items.title: HumanoidTTT: Test-Time Capability Reuse for Efficient Humanoid Control
items.summary: This research introduces "HumanoidTTT," a method for efficient humanoid control through test-time capability reuse, addressing the challenge of reliably re-executing motion capabilities during continuous deployment.

items.title: Toward Humanoid Robots in Construction: A Teleoperation Feasibility Study
items.summary: This study presents a teleoperation system using extended reality (XR) and pedal-based locomotion to enable a single operator to control a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for construction tasks, addressing labor shortages.

items.title: Reactive Humanoid Multi-Contact Using Learned Stability Models
items.summary: This work presents a planning and control approach for reactive humanoid multi-contact, enabling robots to use hand contacts to stabilize themselves in low stability scenarios, preventing falls.

items.title: eRLT: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Learning via Action-Relevant Token Routing
items.summary: This paper introduces eRLT, a method for efficient reinforcement learning in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, specifically for robotic manipulation tasks.

items.title: NarrativeFlow: Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Model Using Robot Velocity Fields
items.summary: NarrativeFlow proposes a flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that uses robot velocity fields for language-conditioned robotic manipulation across various robot platforms.

items.title: quARtet Marker: A 3D-Printable Multi-Tag Fiducial for Robust Near-Frontal Pose Estimation
items.summary: This paper presents the quARtet Marker, a 3D-printable fiducial designed to enhance robust pose estimation for robotic manipulation, especially when dealing with transparent or reflective objects.

items.title: WBAG: A Whole-Body and Attached-Geometry Safety Framework for Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
items.summary: WBAG is a safety framework developed for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies in robotic manipulation, addressing potential collisions involving the robot, objects, and environment.

items.title: MASkillBlender: Decentralized Whole-Body Coordination for Multi-Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Skill Blending
items.summary: MASkillBlender proposes a decentralized whole-body coordination approach for multi-humanoid loco-manipulation, utilizing skill blending to manage complex control and decision-making.

items.title: Recova: Agent-Guided Failure Recovery for Autonomous Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Recova introduces an agent-guided framework for autonomous robotic manipulation that develops both task execution and failure recovery capabilities in reconstructed digital environments.

items.title: EIDA: Execution-Interface Dynamics Adaptation for Real-to-Sim-to-Real Robot Navigation
items.summary: EIDA presents a method for execution-interface dynamics adaptation to improve real-to-sim-to-real transfer for robot navigation by fitting responses from target-platform execution data.

items.title: ColoACT: Multi-Cue Action Chunking for Smooth Autonomous Colon Navigation on a Self-Propelled Endoscopic Robot
items.summary: ColoACT develops multi-cue action chunking for smooth autonomous colon navigation using a self-propelled endoscopic robot, addressing challenges like deformable anatomy and weak textures.

items.title: PROMO: Preference-conditioned Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Quadrupedal Robots
items.summary: PROMO introduces a preference-conditioned multi-objective reinforcement learning approach for quadrupedal robots to balance conflicting objectives like tracking, stability, and energy efficiency.

items.title: Ex vivo breach detection using electrical conductivity during robotic pedicle drilling in the spine
items.summary: This study explores ex vivo breach detection using electrical conductivity during robotic pedicle drilling in the spine, aiming to improve precision and reduce complications in scoliosis surgery.

items.title: Continue, Abort, or Fall: Viability-Aware Policy Selection (VAPS) for Safe Humanoid Acrobatics
items.summary: Viability-Aware Policy Selection (VAPS) is proposed for safe humanoid acrobatics, enabling robots to select policies (continue, abort, or fall) to prevent hardware damage during dynamic motions.

items.title: ALFRED: Requirement-driven development of an open-source mobile manipulator for long-term plant monitoring
items.summary: ALFRED is an open-source mobile manipulator developed for long-term plant monitoring, designed to track seasonal changes in crops and forests using ground robots with manipulation capabilities.

items.title: ReCo: Response-Consistent Locomotion with Policy-Aware MPC for Legged Manipulation
items.summary: ReCo focuses on response-consistent locomotion with policy-aware Model Predictive Control (MPC) for legged manipulation, combining learned policies with MPC to coordinate base and arm movements.

items.summary: Toborlife AI launched TURN, a U.S. reseller network, to expand the availability of Unitree robots to more businesses.

items.summary: Maven Robotics plans to mass-produce its mobile manipulator robot for industrial automation, following a recent $100 million funding round.

items.summary: A new humanoid robot has been developed that is capable of safely working alongside human personnel. This highlights advancements in embodied AI and robotic interaction.

items.summary: China's humanoid robot sector is experiencing rapid growth, with its influence and products expanding globally.

items.title: AdaOcc: Adaptive 3D Occupancy Prediction for Embodied Tasks
items.summary: This paper introduces AdaOcc, a method for adaptive 3D occupancy prediction designed to provide accurate and flexible 3D scene representations for embodied AI tasks.

items.title: Optimize, Learn, Refine: Whole-Body Grasping and Pick-and-Throw with a Spiral Soft Robot
items.summary: This research details an optimization, learning, and refinement approach for enabling a spiral soft robot to perform whole-body grasping and pick-and-throw maneuvers.

items.title: SynIL: Leveraging Synergy for Offline Imitation Learning from Imperfect Demonstration Datasets
items.summary: This research presents SynIL, a method that leverages synergy for offline imitation learning, enabling robots to acquire skills effectively even from imperfect demonstration datasets.

items.title: GestAdapt: Workspace-Conditioned Co-Speech Gesture Generation for Humanoid Robots
items.summary: This research proposes GestAdapt, a method for generating workspace-conditioned co-speech gestures, allowing humanoid robots to adapt their movements to physical environmental constraints.

items.title: Memorize, Adapt, Ignore: Diagnosing Robot Learning Mechanisms under Training Data Variation
items.summary: This paper explores robot learning mechanisms under varying training data, aiming to diagnose how robotic manipulation policies memorize, adapt, or ignore different data inputs for improved robustness.

items.title: Draft: A Parametric Tool for Robot Design Exploration
items.summary: This paper introduces Draft, a parametric tool designed to facilitate robot design exploration by integrating morphology and control iteration, improving the co-design process.

items.title: Embodiment-aware control by inference over the operator: a simulation study
items.summary: This simulation study explores embodiment-aware control in teleoperation systems by inferring operator states to enhance the sense of embodiment with the controlled device.

items.title: CADeT: Causal-Aware Deformation Transmission for Indirect Robotic Manipulation of Soft Tissue
items.summary: This paper introduces CADeT, a causal-aware deformation transmission method for indirect robotic manipulation of soft tissue, particularly in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery.

items.title: What to Attend, What to Keep: Skill-Conditioned Visuotactile Representation with Progress-Guided Event Memory
items.summary: This research investigates skill-conditioned visuotactile representation for robotic manipulation, focusing on how vision and touch guide actions like reaching and grasping, and how "event memory" influences these processes. It aims to improve multi-modal manipulation policies by addressing limitations of fixed temporal contexts.

items.title: Behavioral Persistence and Incomplete Functional Transfer of Co-evolved Communication in Evolutionary Robotics
items.summary: This work evaluates the transfer of a co-evolved communication protocol from a 2D simulation to 3D physical e-puck-type robots in a food-seeking task, without retraining their GRU network weights. It assesses the behavioral persistence and functional transfer of this communication in a physical environment.

items.title: Systematically Exploring the Capabilities of GPT-6 Astra as Embodied Policies
items.summary: This research systematically explores the capabilities of GPT-6 Astra in generating numerical robot actions as general-purpose embodied policies. It evaluates Astra's performance across six domains, examining its direct control and cooperative abilities in robotic tasks.

items.title: Dense Temporal Motion Retargeting for Legged Robots
items.summary: This work presents dense temporal motion retargeting for legged robots, enabling them to learn expressive whole-body skills from human and animal motions. It focuses on adapting complex dynamic movements, like jumps, to the specific morphology and dynamic properties of the robot.

items.title: TERRA: Terrain-Aware Reconstruction, Retargeting and Control for Musculoskeletal Locomotion
items.summary: TERRA introduces a method for terrain-aware reconstruction, retargeting, and control for musculoskeletal locomotion, enabling muscle-actuated agents to reproduce complex human motions. This research aims to overcome limitations of existing systems that are largely confined to flat ground by integrating terrain geometry.

items.title: CEER2: Directional and Tunable End-Effector and Root Compliance for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: This paper presents CEER2, a system for directional and tunable end-effector and root compliance in humanoids for loco-manipulation tasks. It addresses the challenge of physical interaction, allowing robots to respond to external forces while maintaining task-specific motion.

items.title: AIfred: Augmented Learning through Functional Robotic Embodiment at the Desk
items.summary: AIfred is a desk-based robotic system designed to provide augmented learning by integrating generative AI assistance directly into handwritten engagement. It aims to bridge the gap between digital AI guidance and physical learning activities.

items.title: PhaseSync-Exo: Human Clock Anchored Reference Adaptation for Dynamic Gait Tracking
items.summary: PhaseSync-Exo is an exoskeleton system designed for human-aware walking and dynamic gait tracking, utilizing human clock-anchored reference adaptation. It combines IMU-based reconstruction with amplitude-cadence retargeting to preserve human timing under dynamic constraints.

items.title: Coral Grow-out Robotic Assessment System (CGRAS): Scaling Coral Recruit Monitoring Through Robotics and Computer Vision
items.summary: The Coral Grow-out Robotic Assessment System (CGRAS) is proposed to scale coral recruit monitoring for reef restoration efforts. It utilizes robotics and computer vision to address the need for efficient assessment technologies in combating the impacts of climate change on coral reefs.

items.title: Locomotion-Grounded Humanoid Soccer: Task-Gated Reinforcement Learning of a Multi-Directional Kicking Library
items.summary: This research explores locomotion-grounded humanoid soccer, proposing a task-gated reinforcement learning approach for a multi-directional kicking library. It aims to improve humanoid locomotion by training it on a broader range of commands beyond simple motion tracking for ball approach.

items.title: DODGER: Safety-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Robot Navigation Among Dynamic Obstacles
items.summary: DODGER presents a safety-guided reinforcement learning framework for robot navigation among dynamic obstacles in human-centered environments. It uses control barrier functions (CBFs) to enable robots to avoid collisions while learning safe navigation policies.

items.title: Cue the Flow: Steering Flow-Matching Policies for Open-World Delivery Manipulation
items.summary: This research proposes a method for steering flow-matching policies to enable mobile manipulators to perform open-world goods delivery based on user instructions.

items.title: NEXUS: Perceptive Whole-Body Control for Terrain-Adaptive Teleoperation
items.summary: This paper introduces NEXUS, a perceptive whole-body control method for terrain-adaptive teleoperation, allowing a humanoid robot to mimic human behavior across different terrains.

items.title: Function beyond Form: Functional Correspondence for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasp Generation
items.summary: This research addresses cross-embodiment dexterous grasp generation by introducing a functional correspondence concept for robotic hands with varying geometries and kinematics.

items.title: OccluDex: Hierarchical 3D Visuo-Tactile Representation Learning for Egocentric Dexterous Manipulation under Self-Occlusion
items.summary: This paper presents OccluDex, a hierarchical 3D visuo-tactile representation learning approach for egocentric dexterous manipulation that addresses self-occlusion challenges.

items.title: Humanoid Robot Shipments Jump 432%, China Has 95% Market Share - Forbes
items.summary: Shipments of humanoid robots surged by 432%, with China holding 95% of the market share.

items.title: Solving for the hand: Startup wants to pay prosthetic users to teach robots
items.summary: Startup Psyonic plans to collect data from prosthetic hand users in developing nations to advance the development of humanoid robotic hands.

items.title: Innodata opens motion-capture lab to help humanoids move more like people
items.summary: Innodata has opened a motion-capture lab using Vicon cameras to collect sub-millimeter accurate data, helping humanoids learn to move more naturally.

items.summary: Global shipments of humanoid robots surged by 432% in the first half of the year, with China dominating the market and Agibot surpassing Unitree.

items.title: AgiBot Delivers 20,000th Robot as 300-Plus Units Go to Work at Chimelong Spaceship Park
items.summary: AgiBot delivered its 20,000th robot, an Expedition A3 Ultra, to Chimelong, with over 300 units now deployed for daily work at a Zhuhai park.

items.title: Simate Debuts Simate-beta Physical AI Fast System, Says It Tops RoboDojo Benchmark
items.summary: Simate debuted Simate-beta, a fast-reaction physical AI model that reportedly topped the RoboDojo benchmark with a 33.95 average score. The model was developed using an agent-driven research pipeline.

items.title: Passive-Dynamic-Walking-Inspired Dynamics Guidance for Energy-Efficient Humanoid Locomotion
items.summary: This research investigates dynamics guidance inspired by passive-dynamic walking to discover mechanically economical gait coordination for energy-efficient humanoid locomotion using reinforcement learning.

items.title: Scouting the Dynamics Gap: Test-Time Policy Adaptation via Action-Outcome Feedback
items.summary: This research addresses test-time policy adaptation for robotic policies using action-outcome feedback to adapt to unobserved physical properties and dynamics during deployment.

items.title: KPI: A Promptable Kernel for Physical Interaction on Humanoids
items.summary: This item introduces KPI, a promptable kernel for physical interaction on humanoids, designed to provide more detailed information for whole-body tracking policies beyond simple trajectories.

items.title: Test-Time Adaptation of Manipulation Policies Under Actuator Degradation
items.summary: This research focuses on test-time adaptation of robot manipulation policies to account for actuator degradation, ensuring consistent performance despite real-world hardware changes.

items.title: Design and Validation of an Antagonistic Tendon-Driven Dexterous Robotic Hand with Bidirectional Operation
items.summary: This item describes the design and validation of an antagonistic tendon-driven dexterous robotic hand with bidirectional operation, aiming to improve grasping workspace compared to human-like designs.

items.title: One from Infinity: Actualizing Futures from Pretrained World Models into Robot Actions
items.summary: This research proposes a method to actualize specific, task-conditioned futures from pretrained video world models into executable robot actions, enabling robots to realize desired outcomes.

items.title: FineART: Fine-grained Annotated Robotic Trajectory Dataset and Vision-Language-Action Model for Bimanual Manipulation
items.summary: This item introduces FineART, a fine-grained annotated robotic trajectory dataset, and a vision-language-action model designed to support complex, multi-step bimanual manipulation tasks for robots.

items.title: Trajectory-Level Mode Guidance for Controllable Diffusion-Based Multi-Robot Motion Planning
items.summary: This research introduces a method for controllable multi-robot motion planning using diffusion models, enabling the generation of diverse and feasible trajectory solutions for robot coordination.

items.title: Reactive Real-Time Flow Policies via Asynchronous Distribution Alignment
items.summary: This work proposes a method for achieving reactive, real-time control for generalist robot policies, such as Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, by using asynchronous execution to predict future actions while current ones are carried out.

items.title: Planning Oriented 3D Scene Completion via Coupled TUDF Occupancy Representation Learning from Partial Observations
items.summary: This paper addresses challenges in robotic navigation by improving 3D scene completion from partial observations, using a coupled TUDF occupancy representation for better environmental understanding.

items.title: Learning to Explore Hidden Kinematics for Articulated Object Manipulation
items.summary: This research explores a method for robots to learn and identify the hidden kinematics of articulated objects through interaction, enabling more effective manipulation without restricting action choices.

items.title: A robust single-sensing-element tactile sensor for concurrent pressure and tackiness detection with real-time signal decoupling capability
items.summary: This item presents a new robust tactile sensor designed for humanoid robots' artificial skin, capable of concurrently detecting pressure and tackiness with real-time signal decoupling.

items.title: EquivDP3: A SIM(3)-Invariant Point-Cloud Encoder for Data-Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: This work introduces EquivDP3, a SIM(3)-invariant point-cloud encoder designed to improve data efficiency for visuomotor policies in humanoid loco-manipulation tasks by generalizing across object poses.

items.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Vision-Language-Action Models via Reinforced Fine Tuning
items.summary: This study investigates reinforcement learning methods to enable cooperative multi-agent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to achieve fine-grained coordination for inter-robot collaboration.

items.title: Executor-aware Candidate Selection via a Feasibility Certificate
items.summary: This paper presents a certificate-based candidate-selection framework that improves motion planning for modular robotic systems by ensuring the planned motions are compatible with the robot's executor.

items.title: OTRetarget: Joint Robot and Object Motion Retargeting via Optimal Transport
items.summary: This research proposes OTRetarget, a method that uses optimal transport to transfer human motion to humanoid robots, adapting for robot morphology while preserving environmental interactions for loco-manipulation tasks.

items.title: Foundation-Model-Guided Topology-Aware Semantic Risk Fields for Manipulation
items.summary: This work presents a foundation-model-guided, topology-aware semantic risk field to enhance robot motion planning, enabling robots to navigate everyday environments by considering context-dependent semantic risks beyond just collision avoidance.

items.title: Where Predictive Supervision Goes Shapes What VLA Policies Learn
items.summary: This research investigates how the application of predictive supervision impacts what Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies learn, aiming to improve representations that are beneficial for robot control.

items.title: Degeneracy-Orthogonal Geometric Constraints for LiDAR SLAM
items.summary: This research proposes a method using degeneracy-orthogonal geometric constraints to improve LiDAR SLAM for autonomous robot navigation, addressing limitations like unconstrained drift in axially uniform environments.

items.title: LexiconVLA: Learning Reusable Atomic Action Codebooks for Unseen Tasks
items.summary: This work introduces LexiconVLA, a method for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to learn and reuse atomic action codebooks, improving their ability to perform unseen tasks by consistently executing constituent actions across contexts.

items.title: DRHeC: Differentiable Rendering for Hand-Eye Calibration with RGB-Based Gradients
items.summary: This paper presents DRHeC, a new method for differentiable rendering for hand-eye calibration using RGB-based gradients, offering a markerless approach crucial for precision robotic manipulation.

items.title: TaRL: Learning General and Physical Rewards from Tactile Demonstrations
items.summary: This research introduces TaRL, a method for learning general and physical rewards from tactile demonstrations, enabling reinforcement learning agents to acquire complex, contact-rich robotic manipulation behaviors more effectively.

items.title: Spotter: Let the Embodied Model Lead, and the VLM Reflect for It
items.summary: This work explores whether embodied AI models can self-correct from their failures by employing 'Spotter', a system where the embodied model leads and a Vision-Language Model (VLM) reflects on its actions to suggest corrections.

items.title: PreferenceFlow: Test-Time Guidance of Flow-Matching Robot Policies from Human Interventions
items.summary: This research introduces PreferenceFlow, a method for guiding flow-matching robot policies at test-time using human interventions to improve real-world manipulation.

items.title: All Roads Lead to Rome: Flow-driven Multi-Anchor Exploration for Open-Environment Active 3D Mapping
items.summary: This research proposes a flow-driven multi-anchor exploration method for Open-Environment Active 3D Mapping, aiming to improve long-horizon and shortest trajectory exploration for embodied intelligence.

items.title: AeroManip-VLA: Scalable Vision-Language-Action Learning for Aerial Manipulation with RL-Generated Demonstrations
items.summary: This research introduces AeroManip-VLA, a scalable vision-language-action learning approach for aerial manipulators, using RL-generated demonstrations to extend robotic manipulation into 3D workspaces.

items.title: Track-and-Complete: Learning Humanoid Skills from a Single Failed Human Video
items.summary: This research presents Track-and-Complete, a method enabling humanoid robots to learn skills from a single failed human video by leveraging usable trajectory prefixes before task failure.

items.title: ComManip: Overfitting Manipulation Policies to Comfortable Regions
items.summary: This research introduces ComManip, a method to improve robot manipulation policies by overfitting them to "comfortable regions" and reducing reliance on costly large-scale robot demonstrations.

items.title: Beyond Token Importance: Preserving Spatial Scaffolds for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference
items.summary: This research proposes a new approach to VLA inference for robotic manipulation that preserves spatial scaffolds beyond individual token importance, improving efficiency by addressing limitations in current pruning strategies.

items.title: All You Need Is Low Fidelity: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real of Learned Robotic Fish Control
items.summary: This research demonstrates zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for learned robotic fish control, showing that a low-fidelity simulator is sufficient for developing effective controllers for underwater robots.

items.title: BCNav: Bearing-Conditioned Depth Policies for Sound Source Navigation
items.summary: This research presents BCNav, a method using bearing-conditioned depth policies to enable robots to navigate towards sound sources, extending their perception beyond visual fields in unknown environments.

items.title: Multifunctional Locomotion Control of Multi-Jointed BURs with Swimming and gait Capabilities
items.summary: This research focuses on multifunctional locomotion control for multi-jointed biomimetic underwater robots (BURs), enabling them with both swimming and gait capabilities for underwater tasks.

items.summary: Ukraine's Minister of Digital Transformation, Mykhailo Fedorov, expresses a desire to deploy humanoid robots for military operations against Russians within six months.

items.summary: ForceN will provide training on force and torque sensing for humanoids at RoboBusiness, covering their application and methods to prevent damage to robotic systems.

items.summary: Flourish is launching the Flourish One, a $3,555 Raspberry Pi-powered humanoid home robot designed for busy parents to automate chores through personalized, cloud-trained instruction.

items.summary: The founder of robotics company Unitree predicts that embodied intelligence will soon experience a transformative 'ChatGPT moment'.

items.summary: MR. ROBOT and TROOPERS are contributing to humanoid robot training by filming frontline workers performing their jobs. This initiative aims to enhance the capabilities and realism of humanoid robots through real-world observation.

items.summary: LimX Dynamics and Kyland Technology have unveiled a new humanoid robot featuring a fully domestic electronic architecture and microsecond motion control capabilities.

items.summary: Ubtech Robotics is planning a plant in Kazakhstan and a European rollout, amidst a retreat in its shares.

items.summary: Raise Robotics will discuss strategies for scaling field robots and addressing common failure modes at the RoboBusiness conference.

items.summary: The article presents ScaFi, a scalable robotic fish designed to maintain its swimming ability regardless of size. This development focuses on physical robots for aquatic exploration and monitoring.

items.title: Nations Technologies and SIAT Ship N32H785 Humanoid Joint-Motor MCU Reference
items.summary: Nations Technologies and SIAT released an N32H785 dual-core MCU reference for humanoid robot joint-motor drives, featuring specific torque and current loop capabilities.

items.summary: China accounted for 59% of global industrial robot installations in 2025, installing 354,000 units and remaining the world's largest market.

items.summary: Unitree and other humanoid robot companies are aiming to learn from mistakes made by new energy EV startups to shape their market strategies.

items.title: China tightens humanoid patent grip with 60% share - The Korea Herald
items.summary: The article reports that China is increasing its patent holdings in humanoid robotics, indicating developments in the intellectual property landscape surrounding physical robots.

items.title: POIL: Point-based One-Shot Imitation Learning with Stable Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Presents POIL, a point-based one-shot imitation learning framework that uses stable dynamical systems for robotic manipulation. This method aims to transfer demonstrated trajectories to novel objects and execute them reliably.

items.title: Realizability Is Not Enough: Encoding, Liveness, and Auditing of Synthesized Robot Supervisors
items.summary: Explores the challenges beyond formal guarantees for deploying synthesized robot supervisors, focusing on encoding, liveness, and auditing. It addresses the practical implementation of AI systems that coordinate robotic capabilities.

items.title: Policy-Calibrated DAgger: Offline Calibrated Noise Injection for Imitation Learning
items.summary: Presents Policy-Calibrated DAgger, a method using offline calibrated noise injection to mitigate error accumulation in imitation learning for robots. This approach aims to prevent covariate shift and improve the safety of robotic policies.

items.title: Learning-Based Pressure Predictive Control of a Vertebraic Soft Robotic Tail
items.summary: Proposes an LSTM-based pressure predictive control method for a vertebraic soft robotic tail. This research addresses the complex kinematics of soft robots to achieve precise control despite their non-static motions and nonlinear material behavior.

items.title: Tactile Sensing Array for Multi-Phalanx Sensing in Humanoid Hands
items.summary: Presents a tactile sensing array designed for multi-phalanx sensing in humanoid hands. This technology aims to provide comprehensive tactile feedback across the whole finger to improve grasping and object manipulation.

items.title: Aerial Manipulation in the Wild with Onboard Perception, Policy Learning, and Whole-Body Control
items.summary: Introduces a real-world outdoor aerial manipulation framework integrating onboard perception, policy learning, and whole-body control. This system addresses the challenges of reliable state estimation, stable aerial motion, and precise manipulation under external disturbances for drones.

items.title: Containing Behavioral Cascades from Manipulated Claims in LLM-Powered Multi-Robot Systems
items.summary: Investigates how LLM-powered multi-robot systems are vulnerable to semantic manipulation, where false claims can trigger fleet-wide behavioral cascades. This research aims to contain such cascades to prevent issues like unnecessary replanning and increased mission costs.

items.title: GraspTwin: Zero-Shot Task-Oriented Grasp Optimization via a Digital Twin
items.summary: Presents GraspTwin, a method for zero-shot task-oriented grasp optimization for robots using a digital twin. It enables robots to perform complex grasping tasks, like 'pouring coffee,' with an increasing variety of objects.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Prompted Policy Search for Robotic Control

items.summary: This research introduces decision checkpoints to audit scientific-search agents, recording their observations and tool actions to understand where they fail during inference rather than just relying on final answer accuracy.

items.title: Staying on Task: Testing the Foundations of Long-Horizon Agent Reliability
items.summary: This research investigates the reliability of long-horizon agentic workflows, examining how agents sustain state-dependent actions and manage growing context, changing sub-task complexity, and new data.

items.title: STRATA: Self-Learning Through Role-Aligned Tiered Agents for Real-Time Strategy Games
items.summary: This research introduces STRATA, a system of self-learning, role-aligned tiered agents designed to coordinate complex economic, defense, and attack strategies in real-time strategy (RTS) games.

items.title: Consistent Plan-Act for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
items.summary: This paper proposes a 'Consistent Plan-Act' approach to improve reasoning and execution for long-horizon agentic tasks by investigating coordination failures between planning and acting roles.

items.title: Composing Task-specific Agent Harnesses at Test Time with Reusable Primitives
items.summary: This research explores how 'agent harnesses'—mechanisms governing LLM context gathering, tool invocation, and state preservation—can be composed with reusable primitives to optimize performance for diverse tasks.

items.title: TomasuLLM: Out-of-Order Speculative Execution for LLM Agents
items.summary: TomasuLLM proposes an out-of-order speculative execution method to reduce latency in LLM agents, especially when using long-running tools.

items.title: Which Models Work Well Together? Measuring Heterogeneity for LLM Team Selection
items.summary: This research explores methods for measuring heterogeneity and complementarity among large language models to optimize LLM team selection and improve collaborative performance.

items.title: EVOKE: Eliciting World Knowledge in Agents for Transferable Decision-Making
items.summary: EVOKE is a method designed to elicit world knowledge in AI agents, aiming to improve their transferable decision-making capabilities across unseen environments.

items.title: Prompt2Skill: Unsupervised Skill Optimization From Natural Language Instructions
items.summary: Prompt2Skill introduces an unsupervised method for optimizing "skills" for Large Language Models from natural language instructions, aiming to reduce the cost and improve the effectiveness of expert-authored skills for specialized domains. These skills are external artifacts consumed by LLMs to enhance performance.

items.title: Breaking Babel: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Long-Form Subtitle Translation
items.summary: Breaking Babel introduces a self-evolving multi-agent system for long-form subtitle translation, designed to overcome the limitations of single-LLM methods by reasoning over discourse and cultural context and adapting its workflow. items.title: Can Terminal Agents Trust Their Own Verification? Diagnosing and Improving Self-Verification
items.summary: This research investigates the trustworthiness of self-verification in terminal agents that interact with command-line environments, proposing a diagnostic framework to assess and improve their ability to evaluate and correct their own solutions.

items.title: RSIGame: Autonomous Agentic Game Development with Recursive Self-improvement

items.title: False Frontiers: Diagnosing and Mitigating Co-Cheating in Self-Evolving Search Agents
items.summary: This research identifies and analyzes "co-cheating," a failure mode in self-evolving search agents where proposers and solvers increasingly agree on shared errors. It discusses methods for diagnosing and mitigating this issue in agent training curricula.

items.title: DAGent: Evaluate-then-Grow Planning for Deep Research Agents
items.summary: DAGent proposes an "Evaluate-then-Grow" planning method for deep research agents, utilizing Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-based multi-agent systems. This approach enables agents to navigate large knowledge spaces, synthesize evidence, and adapt plans for complex research tasks.

items.title: Contingent Exposure Routing for Financial AI: Outage Risk and the Cost of Indivisible Decisions
items.summary: Model failover restores availability, but changes which financial institutions share decision errors. We formulate outage-contingent routing through a local market-impact response matrix and study expected squared price displacement. A symmetric construction shows that a shared backup can leave an order-one concentration floor as the number of primary endpoints grows, while balanced fallback risk decreases inversely with the surviving endpoint count. For indivisible decisions, we derive the exact second moment of independent randomized routing and an effective-exposure granularity that determines its gap from fractional allocation. Conditional-expectation rounding gives a finite-agent bound without coupled quotas; a separate swap procedure preserves endpoint counts and is assessed against dual lower bounds. Across 60 synthetic portfolio networks and 11,340 scenario evaluations, the latter reduces risk by 6.57% and 10.53% for single and double endpoint removals at the central feedback setting with independent errors. A replay of 1,024 recorded API responses on constructed rebalancing tasks gives a smaller held-out reduction of 3.30% (paired bootstrap interval 2.07--4.57%). Strongly aligned errors, inferior endpoints, and indivisibility limit diversification. The contribution is an auditable routing stress test and implementation analysis, not an estimate of real-market crash probabilities.

items.title: The Null Is the Hard Part: Exact Tests for Memorization in Generative Models
items.summary: Memorization audits of generative models read similarity scores against thresholds, with no null distribution, and the conclusions they support can be wrong. By MemBench's rule, the benchmark's mitigations roughly halve Stable Diffusion's memorization; audited with false-discovery control, two thirds of the certified images are no longer detected under random prompt perturbations, five sixths under attention rescaling, and all of them under embedding optimization. The field's data-copying test, read against its own null, flags ten of twenty-four generators that reproduce nothing. We argue that for memorization the null is the hard part, and supply two. For a whole model, training and held-out images are exchangeable given its samples, and relabelling them is a permutation test, exact for any statistic when the held-out images are a random split; under it, a nearest-neighbour preference still fires on seven of those twenty-four, and a count restricted to the near-duplicate scale on none (McNemar p=0.016). For single images, the natural nulls fail twice, measurably: ranking an image among random images yields 596 false discoveries among 2,365 controls, and resampling independent generations makes the null three times too narrow. Calibrated against matched controls, the audit certifies 36 of 61 MemBench images at 5% false-discovery rate, held-out controls are certified in 0.01% of calibration splits, and on this benchmark two generations per image recover that count. A calibrated maximum, which reads occasional rather than typical copying, certifies 46. As the scale-restricted statistic we recommend the small-scale mass of the Intersection Euler Characteristic Profile, which also counts distinct images copied and tests whether two models copy the same ones.

items.title: Attention Manifolds: Steering or Blocking Language Models by Editing Learned B-Spline Surfaces
items.summary: In standard transformer attention, a source token sends the same value vector to every receiver. The query determines \emph{how much} to attend but not \emph{what} to extract. This work introduces \textbf{attention manifolds}: learned 2D B-spline surfaces $S_d(q_d, k_d)$ that modulate each value dimension based on the query-key interaction. Each surface is a tensor-product cubic B-spline initialized to zero, preserving pretrained behavior. Applied to LLaMA 3.2-1B-Instruct and 3B-Instruct, attention manifolds reduce WikiText-2 validation perplexity by 2--2.5 points with 0.3\% parameter overhead. Across 112 diverse prompts, surfaces change greedy-decoded output for 69\% (1B) to 83\% (3B) of cases, with the strongest effects on ambiguous and polysemous inputs (94--100\% change rate). The surfaces improve output quality: correcting factual errors (\emph{``the CAP theorem has three main components''} $\to$ \emph{``it is impossible to guarantee all three''}), increasing precision (\emph{``impossible to know certain properties''} $\to$ \emph{``impossible to know both position and momentum''}), and adding specificity (a generic quote $\to$ an attributed Saint Augustine citation, consistently at both scales). The learned surfaces are also mechanically editable: inverting a layer's coefficients changes greedy output for 9/10 prompts (KL~0.010), providing a geometric mechanism for model steering. Setting surface coefficients to $-1$ creates ``attention walls'' that block value flow through specific dimensions. In a preliminary experiment, a layer-wide wall redirects an explosive-device prompt from specific instructions to general educational content, suggesting a path toward safety-oriented manifold shaping.

items.title: Large Language Bayes Is Not Reparameterisation-Invariant
items.summary: Large Language Bayes (LLB) answers an informal modelling question by sampling candidate probabilistic programs from a language model, running approximate inference on each, and averaging them with weights proportional to an exponentiated evidence bound. We show that this weighting depends on how a model is written. The log marginal likelihood is invariant to reparameterisation; the evidence bound is not. On eight schools the centered and non-centered programs are the same measure to $5.7\times10^{-14}$, yet their weights differ by $6.1\times$; importance weighting reduces this only to $2.2\times$, and reproducing the inference LLB actually runs, a full-covariance Gaussian matched to the posterior moments, still leaves $1.9\times$ on eight schools and $8.9\times$ in $64$ dimensions. Across likelihood families, dimensions and funnel severities the discrepancy reaches $31.9\times$ and reverses sign, so no single writing is uniformly preferable. It inverts Bayes factors against eight natural competitors, and the induced error in the model posterior, and in any downstream target, is controlled by the spread $\Delta$ of the bound shortfalls through a known sharp Hilbert-distance bound. Across $360$ programs from six language models the parameterisation written ranges from $0\%$ to $100\%$ centered and is stable within a model. Detecting equivalent programs statistically can falsely merge genuinely different models at practical sample budgets; verifying reparameterisations we generate ourselves cannot, and closes the window.

items.title: MOVE: Multimodal Open-world Verification and Expansion for Graph Learning
items.summary: Multimodal graph learning faces a fundamental challenge: new classes may emerge after deployment, while models are trained with a fixed label space. Existing approaches typically detect unknown nodes and use LLMs to generate candidate class descriptions, but they do not determine whether existing classes are insufficient to cover these nodes or whether a generated class is reliable enough to expand the class space. Our empirical study reveals three challenges: multimodal information beyond individual modalities is required for unknown-node identification, LLM-generated class descriptions may not fully capture multimodal class characteristics, and directly adding candidate classes can introduce redundant categories. Based on these observations, we propose MOVE, a multimodal open-world class verification and expansion framework. MOVE identifies nodes that cannot be assigned to existing classes by jointly considering visual tokens, textual attributes, and graph context, leverages a multimodal LLM to generate candidate classes, and selectively expands the class space only when candidates are consistently supported by multimodal evidence without introducing unnecessary categories. Experiments demonstrate that MOVE achieves an average improvement of 11.87\% across unknown recognition, open-domain annotation, and downstream graph learning tasks.

items.title: Coupling Perception and Reasoning in Federated Multimodal Graph Foundation Models
items.summary: Federated multimodal graph foundation models (GFMs) aim to adapt pretrained multimodal models to decentralized graph data, where each client owns a private multimodal graph and cannot share raw information. These models typically combine a multimodal Encoder that extracts semantic evidence from heterogeneous modalities and a graph neural network (GNN) that performs relational reasoning over graph structures. However, existing federated GFM adaptation methods mainly update graph-side modules while keeping the multimodal Encoder frozen, limiting adaptation to \emph{how information is propagated} while fixing \emph{what information is extracted}. Through empirical studies, we reveal that Encoder and GNN adaptations are not independent: Encoder adaptation is affected by graph relations, while cross-client module swapping reveals substantial pairing sensitivity between separately parameterized Encoder and GNN updates. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{FedCORE}, a federated adaptation framework that represents Encoder and GNN updates through a shared low-dimensional latent state. FedCORE jointly optimizes this core from multimodal and structural signals and performs federated evolution directly in the shared state space, preserving compatibility between perception and reasoning adaptations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedCORE reduces the Encoder--GNN pairing gap from $30.6$ to $5.9$, corresponding to an $80.7\%$ reduction over independent joint adaptation.

items.title: The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Distilling the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) into smaller students is a central challenge for efficient deployment. Current approaches face a fundamental tension: optimizing purely for verifiable task rewards (e.g., via GRPO) leads to reward hacking, where students arrive at correct final answers through flawed intermediate logic, while regularizing with soft divergence penalties against a teacher (e.g., KL-based distillation) dilutes task performance and, critically, allows the student to compensate for severe logical violations at one step with high teacher agreement at others. We argue that this averaging is fundamentally misaligned with the nature of reasoning: a chain-of-thought is only as valid as its weakest link. Motivated by this observation, we formulate reasoning distillation as a constrained reinforcement learning problem in which the task reward is maximized subject to a worst-case constraint on the teacher log-likelihood along every prefix of the trajectory. To avoid the prohibitive cost of dual Lagrangian solvers and the test-time teacher dependence of state-augmented methods such as Saute, we derive an unaugmented constrained MDP whose reward transformation preserves the hard-constraint semantics, admits a low-variance policy gradient decomposition into single-step and long-term terms, and provably satisfies the worst-case constraint almost surely in the penalty limit. Through extensive experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks, we demonstrate that our method significantly expands the accuracy-fidelity Pareto front. By matching the high Final Answer Correctness of pure RL and drastically reducing teacher constraint violations, we ultimately achieve the highest rigorous Reasoning Success Rate across all evaluated settings.

items.title: Benchmarking System One decision models against trained classifiers and language models for automated decision gates
items.summary: Software that hands branching decisions to a model needs a declared option and a probability it can threshold. Typed decision models, also called System One models, return such probabilities without generating text, while supervised classifiers and generative language models are the established alternatives. Under matched conditions, one harness sends eight decision-model checkpoints from six families, including the hosted model Jev, and two generative comparators the same semantic requests, and scores supervised and zero-shot classifiers on the same workflow, intent and social-science items. The ranking of the model classes depends on the conditions. With the task's own labels, small trained classifiers are the most accurate on intents and not significantly different from the best decision models on workflows. Without labels, every decision model except the encoder-based checkpoints exceeds a zero-shot entailment classifier on workflows and intents. Read through option-key likelihoods, a larger generative model is level with Jev on workflows and intents and accepts more workflow decisions at five percent risk, and fine-tuned decision checkpoints gain intent accuracy over their untuned backbones. Stored temperatures fitted on few options raise calibration error with many options, and a held-out threshold for five percent in-scope risk still lets Jev accept 0.310 of out-of-scope requests. Swapping yes and no flips 50.5 answers per hundred for Jev, while fine-tuned checkpoints cut their backbones' social-science flips. An intent-trained first stage escalating to Jev matches its accuracy at 0.43 of its cost at full graphics-processor utilization. The results yield condition-dependent design rules for automated decision gates.

items.title: Deep Learning for Anomaly Detection in Railway Systems: A Structured Survey
items.summary: Ensuring safe and reliable operation of modern railway systems increasingly relies on data-driven monitoring and intelligent fault detection. Deep learning has emerged as an effective paradigm for railway anomaly detection, driven by the growing availability of heterogeneous sensor data from rolling stock and infrastructure. This paper presents a structured survey of deep learning-based anomaly detection approaches for railway systems. The surveyed methods are organized using a unified taxonomy covering anomaly location, data representation and manifestation, sensing modality, and temporal characteristics. Existing approaches, including convolutional, recurrent and attention-based architectures, autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, and transformers, are structured into classification-based, prediction-based, reconstruction-based, and hybrid learning paradigms. The survey also examines data-centric challenges, evaluation practices, performance metrics, and practical deployment aspects, including edge-cloud architectures, computational constraints, and hardware-aware optimization. Finally, a decision-oriented framework links anomaly characteristics, data properties, and operational constraints to suitable detection paradigms and deployment configurations. This work provides a structured reference for selecting and deploying deep learning solutions for railway anomaly detection and highlights open challenges toward reliable and scalable intelligent monitoring systems.

items.title: Manifold-Constrained Initial Noise Optimization for Efficient Generative Model Alignment
items.summary: Recent advances in distillation and flow-map models have enabled deterministic one- or few-step generation for high-quality data, facilitating a new branch of reward alignment approaches that directly optimize the initial noise from a Gaussian distribution. However, most existing initial-noise optimization methods rely on first-order gradient information, which is either inapplicable or suffers from instability and inefficiency in black-box reward scenarios. Here, we introduce ZeNOVA, a stable and efficient initial noise alignment method in a gradient-free manner. Specifically, we address existing algorithms' major challenge in black-box scenarios through annealed soft-value guidance, manifold-constrained hyperspherical Langevin dynamics, and Metropolis-Hastings jumping. Extensive experiments on image and video generative models show that ZeNOVA outperforms all evaluated zeroth-order baselines by optimizing the initial noise toward higher rewards substantially more stably while exploiting the geometry of the Gaussian prior, demonstrating its practical applicability to various black-box reward alignment.

items.title: MoRA: MoE Pruning via Router Bias Learning and Expert Approximation
items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models enable parameter scaling with limited per-token computation by activating only a small subset of experts for each token, but deploying them still requires loading the complete expert pool into memory. Structured expert pruning can effectively reduce the memory usage by removing experts. However, existing pruning methods either use expert ranking criteria that are not well aligned with model performance or rely on effective expert subset searching that is computationally expensive. Moreover, these methods typically overlook the routing-behavior redundancy among the retained experts. In this paper, we propose MoE Pruning via Router Bias Learning and Expert Approximation (MoRA), a framework for structured MoE expert pruning. We introduce a learnable router bias for each expert and optimize these biases by minimizing the language-modeling loss and a routing-diversity regularizer. The learned router biases sharpen the routing probability distributions to identify experts critical to model performance while encouraging the selection of experts with diverse routing preferences. In addition, we introduce an expert approximation mechanism as a post-pruning enhancement. It leverages the remaining experts to approximate the outputs of pruned experts by affine transformation, further improving the performance of the pruned model. We evaluate MoRA on Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and Moonlight-16B-A3B, removing 25\% and 50\% of the routed experts in each MoE layer. Extensive experiments on nine zero-shot benchmarks show that MoRA outperforms state-of-the-art pruning algorithms. Our code will be released.

items.title: When Do Attention-Head Ablations Support Causal Claims? Projection-Level Confounds, Floor Effects, and Matched Controls
items.summary: Attention-head ablation, zeroing a head and measuring the resulting change in task performance, is a common method for inferring which components of a language model are causally responsible for a behavior. We show using GPT-2 small that this inference can be fragile unless the intervention semantics, evaluation metric, and controls are carefully validated. A natural post-projection implementation of "zeroing a head" is nearly uncorrelated with a corrected pre-projection ablation (Pearson r = 0.057) and selects a completely disjoint top-5 set of important heads. We also show that binary accuracy can hide effects at behavioral floors and near ceilings, whereas gold-token log-probability remains graded. Using a discovery/held-out split and 1,000 matched random-head and layer-matched-head control draws, the corrected per-head effect ranking is highly stable across splits (Spearman rho = 0.974), and the top-5 selected heads significantly exceed both control distributions (Monte Carlo p = 0.001). However, evidence for task specificity is not robust on GPT-2. Replication on DistilGPT2 preserves the intervention-semantic and matched-control findings. These results show that single-head ablation does not by itself justify a causal claim; defensible interpretation requires correct intervention placement, a non-saturated continuous metric, and matched held-out controls.

items.title: A First Glance at Jev for Network Traffic Classification: Accuracy, Processing Time, and Cost
items.summary: We evaluate Jev on ten dataset-defined application labels in CESNET-QUICEXT-25 using only the first ten packets' sizes, directions, and inter-packet times. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first empirical study of general-purpose decision models, represented here by Jev, for application classification of network flows. Across 52,000 records from 26 collection weeks following the training period, 40 fixed labeled examples raise Jev's accuracy from 9.80% to 28.42%. Random Forest and Extra Trees trained on 8,000 records achieve 69.95% and 66.80% and outperform Jev in every week. Increasing Jev's context to 150 examples yields 34.50% on the first test week. On a paired 100-record subset, Jev with 40 examples achieves 29% accuracy at a median request time of 0.750 s, versus 37% and 6.036 s for the generative language model OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol with high reasoning effort through Azure; Jev also incurs lower API charges. The paired subset does not establish an accuracy advantage for either service, and the timing reflects different service configurations. Thus, labeled examples substantially improve Jev, but the tested Jev configurations remain less accurate than trained tree ensembles; unequal supervision budgets and fixed configurations prevent attributing the gap to a single cause.

items.title: STCFormer: Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Modeling with Dynamic Cluster Transformer for Station-based Weather Forecasting
items.summary: Station-based weather forecasting supports daily life and economic activity, yet accurate forecasts require modeling complex spatial dependencies among stations. Recent clustering-based selective modeling offers a promising alternative to dense inter-station interactions. However, a grouping shared across an observation window may obscure local changes in station relationships, while intra-cluster interactions alone may miss important global context. The theoretical advantages of selective interactions over dense connectivity also remain insufficiently understood. We therefore propose STCFormer, an adaptive spatio-temporal Transformer that dynamically groups stations according to their local evolution within each temporal patch. Its Cluster-Guided Attention Block combines fine-grained local attention within clusters and global attention over regional state summaries, allowing each station to access information beyond its own cluster. We further show that a derived Lipschitz upper bound for cluster-conditioned local attention is no larger than its fully connected counterpart, explaining a potential robustness benefit and motivating the design of InfoLoss. Experiments on three real-world weather datasets spanning eight temperature and wind forecasting tasks show that STCFormer achieves the lowest 24-hour mean squared error on all eight tasks and ranks first or second in 47 of 48 comparisons across metrics and forecasting horizons. Ablations and case studies further confirm the benefits of locally adaptive grouping and complementary local-global interactions. Our code can be obtained at https://github.com/hnu-vis/STCFormer.

items.title: Fusion techniques of time frequency-based images to predict the outcome of rTMS depression therapy
items.summary: Depression is a mental condition that can lead to suicide and self-harm. Predicting the outcome of depression treatment is one of the most difficult tasks for clinicians. Among various treatment options, repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is a widely used non-invasive method. Predicting rTMS response using Electroencephalogram (EEG) data is difficult because of high inter-subject variability and limited features from single-domain analysis. We introduce two fusion techniques, montage and blending, to overcome these limitations and extract richer features from EEG-derived Time-Frequency (TF) images. We then propose a lightweight custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on fused TF representations. \textcolor{black}{We use a primary dataset of 15 patients and a secondary dataset of 46 patients. We run two sets of experiments. The first set uses segment-level 10-fold cross-validation. In this setup segments from the same patient can appear in both training and testing. The Montage CWT\_ST fusion reaches 99.90\% accuracy on the primary dataset and 91.90\% on the secondary dataset. The second set uses strict subject-disjoint cross-validation. All segments of a patient stay in one fold and no patient appears in both training and testing. Performance collapses. We test four time-frequency methods, six fusion mechanisms, and fourteen model architectures. With one exception, every configuration on both cohorts falls between AUC 0.31 and 0.54 and every 95\% confidence interval contains 0.5. A patient-level permutation test on the best standalone method returns $p = 0.703$. The best subject-level result is Montage CWT\_ST on the primary cohort, which reaches AUC $0.874 \pm 0.183$ and 82.7\% accuracy.

items.title: OmniMed-Jev: Calibrating LVLM Confidence for Trustworthy Medical Multimodal Decisions via System One
items.summary: Medical models are judged not only on correctness, but on whether reported confidence matches actual accuracy. Generalist multimodal medical models have expanded what a single model can perceive, yet they still express bounded decisions such as diagnoses, findings or cell counts as generated text, so the reported probability reflects the next token rather than the decision itself. Motivated by decision-native interfaces such as Jev, we introduce OmniMed-Jev, which represents each medical decision as a Choice, Noul or Score decision over a runtime-supplied candidate set and returns a full distribution over that set: mutually exclusive classes, binary presence of a finding, or a bounded ordered value. The design is omni in three respects: it accepts diverse imaging modalities, covers different prediction tasks, and expresses them through one candidate-conditioned probability model, so heterogeneous outputs become comparable probabilities rather than task-specific strings. In an interface-controlled comparison against a generative baseline trained on the same backbone, data and schedule, OmniMed-Jev's reported probabilities track observed correctness far more closely, reducing calibration error by up to an order of magnitude and reliability error by up to two, while point-prediction performance remains comparable; counting is the one family where the generative baseline stays ahead. Making the decision distribution the model's output is not a format change but what turns reported numbers into probabilities that mean what they say. These results support explicit decision modeling as a way to make reported confidence meaningful within the evaluated tasks, and they are not evidence of clinical readiness: the comparison cannot separate the interface from associated training differences, which we state alongside the results. Code is available at github.com/lytang63/OmniMed-Jev.

items.title: FAER: Auditable Utility-Aligned Trajectory Replay for Language Model Post-Training
items.summary: Replay selectors often rank cached trajectories by format feedback, confidence, freshness, or response length, although cache-level correctness and downstream learner utility are distinct objectives. We formalize this selection-to-learning gap and introduce FAER as an auditable full-trajectory replay framework. Its training-free fixed selector is a protocol baseline; FAER-UTILITY is the learner-aware selector fitted on disjoint calibration blocks. The normalized gradient alignment is reported as a baseline, while a disposable optimizer-aware virtual update supplies a magnitude-aware utility surface. The audit contract freezes observed fields and replay traces before evaluation labels are joined. On GSM8K with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, the matched learner study reports quality 0.6329 for the fixed selector, compared with 0.5482 for uniform and 0.6037 for format-feedback under 128 updates. Metadata-only cross-fitted calibration reaches $0.6476\!\pm\!0.0139$ over eight seeds (median 0.6481; paired 95% interval $[+0.079,+0.122]$) at 63,276 target-run tokens; its recorded full cost is 189,642 tokens and 3.48 GPU-hours including calibration. The completed FAER-UTILITY row reaches 0.6624 at 62,844 target-run tokens and 4.26 GPU-hours. Format-feedback selects records with correctness 0.6953, compared with 0.3594 for the fixed selector, despite the different downstream ranking. The completed comparison surfaces report the learner-aware ablation, same-seed gap, policy-optimization rows, and strict zero-shot transfer.

items.title: T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Reinforcement learning enables large language model (LLM) agents to learn multi-step behaviors through interaction with their environments. However, rewards in many interactive tasks reflect only the final outcome, providing limited guidance on which intermediate decisions advance the task. Successful training trajectories contain intermediate states that can provide supervision for subsequent interactions. We introduce Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization (T2SPO), a method that uses past interaction trajectories to provide step-level feedback for policy learning. T2SPO derives remaining-distance targets from successful trajectories and pairs them with representations of the states visited along the way. Conditioned on these examples, a pretrained TabPFN regressor estimates the remaining distance to success at each state of a new rollout. Changes in this distance estimate across consecutive states yield auxiliary credit for agent steps alongside task-level supervision. As training proceeds, newly completed trajectories refresh the estimator's context, incorporating new experience without updating its parameters. Experiments with 1.5B and 7B language models on ALFWorld and WebShop show that T2SPO consistently improves overall task success over GRPO.

items.title: MatrixReward: Reward from Rubric Matrix for Open-Ended Generation
items.summary: Open-ended query generation lacks standard answers, thus necessitating an effective reward mechanism. Pointwise scoring rubrics provide limited information about the relative quality of sample answers under the same prompt; merging multiple rubric judgments into a single score may also mask the differences between these answers. We propose MatrixReward, which constructs rewards from a rollout-by-rubric win-rate matrix obtained by comparing every pair of sampled responses under each rubric. The spread of each matrix column captures how strongly that rubric distinguishes the current rollouts, while correlations between columns reveal rubric repetition; together, these statistics yield data-dependent rubric weights. We combine these weights with the prior weights of rubrics. After column normalization and weighting, the observed per-rubric maxima and minima define positive and negative ideal profiles. Each rollout's distances to these two ideals determine its relative-closeness quality reward. Evaluated using Qwen3-8B on four open-ended query-answering benchmarks, MatrixReward achieves an average score of 63.02, outperforming the strongest baseline by approximately 2.0%. These results support the idea that matrices derived from relative comparisons can be used to construct rewards more reasonably for open-ended generative reinforcement learning.

items.title: Interpretable Synthetic Medical Tabular Data Generation for Clinical Decision Support Using Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
items.summary: Synthetic medical tabular data generation has become essential for developing and validating computer-based medical systems (CBMSs) when real clinical data is restricted due to privacy, ethical, or data availability limitations. Existing probabilistic and deep generative models often lack interpretability and fail to preserve clinically meaningful dependencies, limiting their suitability for safety-critical applications. This paper proposes a novel application of Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs) in a framework for synthetic medical tabular data generation with explicit causality and privacy preservation. Clinical features are described using linguistically interpretable fuzzy sets, and inter-feature dependencies are encoded as FCM edge weights computed from fuzzy set intersections. Synthetic patient records are generated by propagating randomly initialized linguistic activation vectors through the FCM until convergence, followed by defuzzification to produce clinically coherent numerical values. The approach natively handles mixed data types, and domain constraints common in health records. Experimental evaluation on UCI medical benchmark datasets demonstrates competitive performance under a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) protocol. The proposed method achieves accuracy of up to 0.81 and AUROC of up to 0.90 on the Heart Disease dataset, matching or exceeding TVAE and Gaussian Copula baselines while running exclusively on CPU. Fidelity metrics including KS Complement (up to 0.91) and Correlation Similarity (up to 0.95) confirm strong statistical coherence, and DCR Baseline Protection scores consistently exceed those of TVAE, confirming adequate privacy guarantees. These results demonstrate that causally grounded, interpretable fuzzy modeling offers a computationally efficient and transparent alternative to deep generative models for trustworthy synthetic data generation in CBMSs.
