items.title: How ‘Industry 5.0’ integrates human expertise with artificial intelligence - scmp.com
items.summary: The article examines 'Industry 5.0' and how this framework integrates human expertise with artificial intelligence in industrial applications.

items.title: The Unglamorous Work Behind Enterprise AI
items.summary: The article discusses the practical, often 'unglamorous' work involved in implementing and operating AI tools within enterprise settings.

items.title: AI broke the job application. What replaces it?
items.summary: The article discusses how the use of AI by job candidates for creating resumes and cover letters is forcing businesses to rethink their hiring processes.

items.title: Neurosymbolic Routing for Reliable Reasoning on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices
items.summary: This research explores methods for reliable reasoning using small language models on resource-constrained edge devices, addressing challenges in tasks like arithmetic and logic.

items.title: Is Human-Readable Text Necessary for Effective LLM Fine-Tuning?
items.summary: This paper investigates whether human-readable text is essential for effective LLM fine-tuning, proposing a new method (DASA) that uses non-human-readable training representations.

items.title: Self-discovering RL in the Era of Experience: Is Learning History an Asset or a Burden?
items.summary: This paper investigates recursive self-improvement in AI, particularly within reinforcement learning and language model scaling, questioning the role of learning history.

items.title: Mirror-Score: Calibrated, Inference-only Scoring Exposes the Limits of Sequence-compatibility Ranking in D-peptide Design
items.summary: Mirror-Score introduces a new inference-only scoring method to evaluate computational D-peptide designs, exposing limitations in existing sequence-compatibility ranking.

items.title: The Layer Mystery of VLA: An Information-Theoretical Analysis of VLA Latent Interface
items.summary: This research provides an information-theoretical analysis of the 'latent interface' in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, investigating optimal layer selection for action generation.

items.title: AdaST: Adaptive Coupling for Spatial-Temporal Forecasting
items.summary: AdaST proposes an adaptive coupling method for spatial-temporal forecasting, addressing the varying coupling regimes observed in real-world data from systems like traffic and energy networks.

items.title: Principled Thoughts for Latent Recursive LLM Systems
items.summary: This theoretical paper explores fundamental principles for 'latent recursive LLM systems,' discussing how large language models can reason in continuous space using hidden states, potentially involving agents.

items.title: ChronoSRL: Temporal Geometry for Self-Supervised Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces ChronoSRL, a self-supervised reinforcement learning method that measures distances in representation space in units of time to improve goal-reaching in complex environments.

items.title: CoRe: Co-Evolving Reward Models for Mitigating Latent Reward Hacking in Video Diffusion Models
items.summary: This research introduces CoRe, a method using co-evolving reward models to mitigate latent reward hacking, a problem where video diffusion models optimize for high rewards without improving perceptual or motion quality.

items.title: From Surfaces to Volumes: Registered Geometry for Protein Representation Learning
items.summary: This research explores representing protein geometry using registered volumetric organization rather than just surface features to improve protein representation learning.

items.title: Illusory Truth or Mere Exposure? Model-Dependent Repetition Effects in LLM-Based Social Media Simulations
items.summary: This study uses generative agent-based models to simulate social media dynamics and investigate how repetition effects and cognitive biases like the Illusory Truth Effect manifest in LLM agents.

items.title: Towards an AI Software Factory for Data Systems
items.summary: This paper outlines progress towards an 'AI Software Factory' designed to accelerate all stages of the software development lifecycle for data systems using AI-assisted coding tools.

items.title: HyperZip: Efficient Data Compression through Personalized Diffusion LLMs with Hypernetworks
items.summary: HyperZip proposes an efficient LLM-based compression framework that leverages personalized diffusion LLMs with hypernetworks for lossless data compression, addressing computational costs and throughput.

items.title: From Retrieval to Reasoning: Agentic Mechanism Prediction from Cell Painting Profiles
items.summary: This research explores using an agentic approach for mechanism prediction from Cell Painting profiles to advance biological inference, moving beyond simple representation matching.

items.title: Bits Under ZK-LLM: Evaluating Zero-Knowledge-Friendly Quantization for Verifiable Private LLM Inference
items.summary: This research evaluates zero-knowledge-friendly quantization techniques to enable private and verifiable inference for large language models, allowing for auditing while protecting proprietary model parameters.

items.title: Rethinking Reasoning Paths as Phase-Structured Trajectories
items.summary: This paper proposes a method to analyze hidden states within large language models' multi-step reasoning paths, treating them as phase-structured trajectories to improve problem-solving.

items.title: Human-AI Collaboration: From Paradoxes to Patterns
items.summary: This paper examines human-AI collaboration by studying two design dimensions, autonomy and initiative, to identify patterns that lead to better joint performance.

items.title: Visual sensitivity is not claim retractability: persistence-aware credit assignment for multimodal reinforcement learning
items.summary: This paper investigates credit assignment for multimodal reinforcement learning with Large Vision-Language Models, arguing for persistence-aware methods over simple visual sensitivity.

items.title: Sage: Formalization with Semantic Correction
items.summary: Sage is a system for formalizing natural language into formal mathematical statements using neural theorem provers, addressing the challenge of semantic correction and data bottlenecks.

items.title: Serverless gossip training of LSTM failure detectors: A matched-protocol comparison with federated, local and centralized learning on NASA C-MAPSS
items.summary: This study compares serverless gossip training for LSTM failure detectors against federated, local, and centralized learning on NASA C-MAPSS data for industrial predictive maintenance.

items.title: Learning from the Gap Between Pass@K and Pass@1
items.summary: This paper investigates learning from the performance gap between Pass@K and Pass@1 in large language models trained with reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards, analyzing strategies for test-time scaling.

items.title: Calibration-First Cross-Cohort Multimodal Temporal Learning for Transferable Asthma-Risk Forecasting
items.summary: CALIBRA is a novel approach for transferable asthma-risk forecasting using multimodal temporal learning that prioritizes calibration across changing patient populations and sensor ecosystems.

items.title: Binarization Flattens the Score Space
items.summary: This research explores how binarizing rewards from large language model judges impacts the score space, affecting how well a response's criteria are captured.

items.title: HeadGuard: Selective Head Protection for Low-Bit VLM KV-Cache Quantization
items.summary: HeadGuard is a new composable method that uses selective head protection to mitigate degradation in vision-language model accuracy caused by low-bit KV-cache quantization.

items.title: Learned Compression of SAR Phase-History Data: A Rate-Honest Feasibility Study on GOTCHA
items.summary: This study evaluates the feasibility of using a learned convolutional autoencoder for on-board compression of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) phase-history data, comparing it to block-adaptive quantization.

items.title: A Mesoscopic View of Transformer Weights Through Row and Column Scale Fields
items.summary: This paper offers a mesoscopic view of Transformer weights by analyzing row and column scale fields, providing insights into magnitude distribution across functional channels.

items.title: Position: Let's Strengthen Verifiability If We Can't Enforce Reproducibility
items.summary: This position paper argues for strengthening the verifiability of results in machine learning research, given the increasing difficulty in enforcing reproducibility.

items.title: Beyond Keywords: Leveraging Generative LLMs and Label Aggregation to Classify Economic Policy Uncertainty in News Articles
items.summary: This research adapts Large Language Models (LLMs) to automatically classify economic policy uncertainty in news articles for public sector monitoring, moving beyond traditional keyword-based methods.

items.title: ReLOBGen: Replayable Limit Order Book Message Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces ReLOBGen, a method for generating replayable limit order book (LOB) messages essential for closed-loop market simulation. It addresses the issue of non-replayable messages produced by existing generators.

items.title: Hybrid Ensemble Learning for EEG-Based Epileptic Seizure Forecasting
items.summary: This research proposes a calibrated hybrid ensemble learning method that combines five deep learning models for patient-independent EEG-based epileptic seizure forecasting. It aims to improve generalization and false-alarm control.

items.title: From Static Policies to Adaptive Priors in Offline Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper argues for supplementing offline reinforcement learning with adaptive priors, moving beyond static policies, to enhance robustness and address uncertainty outside the offline dataset.

items.title: Learning in the Transverse Subspace: A Minimal Representation for Divergence-Free Operator Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces a minimal representation method for learning divergence-free operators by performing learning in the transverse subspace. This approach reduces redundancy in parameterizations for systems like incompressible flows and PDE systems.

items.title: The Decision Value of Perception Compute
items.summary: This paper defines the 'decision value of perception compute' as the change in downstream loss resulting from improved perception output within an adaptive perception system. It analyzes how perception computation affects downstream decision systems.

items.title: Replication Failure and Trivial Baselines in Road-Level Crash Prediction
items.summary: This study investigates the stability of gains reported by graph neural networks for road-level crash prediction, finding replication failures and issues with trivial baselines in a recent uncertainty-aware model.

items.title: Graph neural networks for sampling-invariant embeddings of organized signal sets
items.summary: This paper investigates the use of graph neural networks to generate sampling-invariant embeddings for organized signal sets, such as those from sensor networks and radars, where individual signals may have distinct sampling parameters.

items.title: KernelOnet: An Interpretable Neural Operator Based on Kernel Functions
items.summary: This paper introduces KernelOnet, an interpretable neural operator framework that integrates kernel functions into its architecture to align with kernel-expansion methods. It offers a new approach to neural operators.

items.title: EnJoi: Ensemble Joint Score Filter for Generative Data Assimilation
items.summary: This paper proposes EnJoi, an Ensemble Joint Score Filter, for generative data assimilation, which utilizes score-based models to generate physically consistent trajectories that align with observations.

items.title: FluxLite: Inference-Time Proposal Control for Discrete Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper introduces FluxLite, a method for inference-time proposal control in discrete diffusion models, addressing challenges with Feynman-Kac sequential Monte Carlo by improving weight stability.

items.title: ROSS: Relearning from Self-Generated Rollouts through Selective Supervision
items.summary: This paper proposes ROSS, a method for relearning from self-generated rollouts through selective supervision during large language model post-training with reinforcement learning. It aims to preserve useful behaviors from historical data.

items.title: Making Cross-Continental Federated Learning Repeatable with FLIP: a Multi-Application Study
items.summary: This paper introduces FLIP (Federated Learning Interoperability Platform), an open-source, multi-application platform designed to make cross-continental federated learning repeatable, particularly addressing governance challenges in healthcare collaborations.

items.title: Neural networks for spectral optimization
items.summary: This paper proposes two neural network models for efficiently solving spectral optimization problems, aiming to find a domain that optimizes a functional dependent on a differential operator's spectrum.

items.title: Improving scalable oversight with co-trained monitors
items.summary: This research explores co-training monitors alongside workers in AI oversight setups to prevent monitor evasion. It investigates both supervised and self-supervised approaches to improve scalable AI oversight.

items.title: ABC: Advantage-Based Control Variates for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: This paper introduces ABC (Advantage-Based Control Variates), a new technique for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. It aims to improve critic-free policy-gradient methods and address approximation error in actor-critic methods.

items.title: Understanding Decision-Making Mechanisms in Neural Routing Solvers
items.summary: This paper investigates the internal decision-making mechanisms of neural routing solvers in Neural Combinatorial Optimization (NCO), examining how autoregressive models like AM and POMO arrive at their decisions.

items.title: GEM-KMeans: Memory-Efficient and Accurate Clustering on Massive Scale with GPU Optimization
items.summary: This paper introduces GEM-KMeans, a memory-efficient and accurate clustering method for massive-scale data, which utilizes GPU optimization and non-negative low-rank matrix factorization for K-means.

items.title: Early Learning Shapes Later Directions Of Representation Change In Continual Learning
items.summary: This research investigates how early representational changes in neural networks form a geometric structure that influences later learning in continual learning tasks. It identifies a low-dimensional subspace of early representation drift, termed a scaffold, that shapes subsequent learning.

items.title: PHASE: A Physiology-Guided Hierarchical Foundation Model for Intracranial EEG
items.summary: PHASE is a physiology-guided hierarchical foundation model designed for analyzing intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) data. It learns by reconstructing or predicting input based on directly measurable physiological characteristics, aiding clinicians and neuroscientists.

items.title: Data Unlearning via Inverse Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces Inverse Distillation Unlearning (IDU), a unified framework designed to enable multi-step matching models, such as flow and diffusion models, to unlearn unwanted components from their training datasets. IDU also aims to simultaneously distill these models to reduce inference costs.

items.title: LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks
items.summary: LoopICL is a new looped transformer architecture designed to efficiently solve tabular tasks using in-context learning. Its core design decouples parameters, aiming to address redundancy observed in current tabular foundation models.

items.title: Koa-action: Fast and Consistent Structured Decision Making with Generative LLMs
items.summary: Koa-action is a method aimed at enabling fast and consistent structured decision-making using generative large language models (LLMs). It addresses the challenge of low-latency classification in industry applications where current LLM approaches are often too slow.

items.title: ThinQuant: Scalable Rotation Learning for Weight and Activation Quantization of LLMs
items.summary: ThinQuant is a method for scalable rotation learning used in the weight and activation quantization of large language models (LLMs). It aims to enable low-bit quantization by smoothing outliers in the activation distribution, improving efficiency.

items.title: Reasoning with Neural Cellular Automata
items.summary: This work investigates the reasoning capabilities of Neural Cellular Automata (NCAs) for visual reasoning tasks, proposing them as a decentralized alternative to traditional AI architectures that rely on global connectivity.

items.title: Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This paper introduces "Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding," a method designed to improve parallel speculative drafting in LLMs by addressing inconsistent continuations that can shorten accepted prefixes. It aims to enhance the speed and quality of text generation.

items.title: Fair Policy Optimization in Major-Minor Weakly Coupled Markov Decision Processes
items.summary: This research focuses on fair policy optimization within major-minor weakly coupled Markov decision processes (M2WCMDPs) for sequential decision-making environments. It addresses resource allocation fairness by considering coupled action spaces under resource constraints.

items.title: EvoMO-SR: Multiobjective LLM-based Evolution of Symbolic Expressions with substructure guidance
items.summary: EvoMO-SR is a multiobjective, Large Language Model-based method for Symbolic Regression (SR), designed for scientific discovery. It utilizes LLMs with substructure guidance to search for interpretable analytical relationships within data.

items.title: Physical Cross-Modal Masked Autoencoding for Seismic-to-Well Representation Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes "Physical Cross-Modal Masked Autoencoding" for seismic-to-well representation learning, aiming to align diverse modalities in scientific measurements. It addresses the dense-sparse problem in subsurface characterization using 3D seismic and well log data.

items.title: Representable but Unlearned: Encoding Rank and the Interaction-Prediction Floor
items.summary: This research investigates how input encodings can limit the measured contrasts a predictor can jointly reproduce, even when no single contrast is forced to vanish. It computes the attainable contrast space from an encoder's equivalence classes and a fixed contrast design.

items.title: On the spectral properties of generative denoiser Jacobians
items.summary: This paper examines the spectral properties of generative denoiser Jacobians in models like diffusion and flow-matching, which learn to sample from complex distributions. It provides a deeper analytical understanding of these generative denoising models.

items.title: EnergyEminence: Source-Aware Environmental Calibration and Evaluation in a Physics-Grounded Grid Digital Twin
items.summary: EnergyEminence is an early-stage testbed for a physics-grounded digital twin of power grids, designed for source-aware environmental calibration and evaluation. It combines data-driven prediction with physically meaningful state evolution for an IEEE 118-bus-style grid.

items.title: Preconditioned Physics-Informed Neural Operator Training
items.summary: This paper introduces "Preconditioned Physics-Informed Neural Operator Training," a method to train neural operators purely from governing physics equations. This approach eliminates the need for large offline datasets typically generated by classical solvers.

items.title: How Language Models Differ in Redistributing Attention-Head Activity Under Serial Demand
items.summary: This research investigates how language models redistribute activity across their attention heads in response to varying serial task demands. It offers insight into how these models route information through their depth, contributing to a mechanistic understanding.

items.title: BASE: Batch-Aware Selection of Experts Using Predicted Removal Error for Efficient MoE Decoding
items.summary: BASE (Batch-Aware Selection of Experts) is a method for efficient decoding in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models. It aims to reduce the computational cost of serving LLMs by optimizing the selection of experts and mitigating bottlenecks in autoregressive decoding.

items.title: The Role of Feed-Forward Layers in Transformer Dynamics
items.summary: This research studies the dynamical behavior of tokens within transformers from a control-theoretic perspective, specifically focusing on the role of feed-forward layers. It interprets the self-attention mechanism as an interacting particle system.

items.title: Can Representation Learning Decouple from Loss Minimization? Polar Updates Have an Answer
items.summary: Investigates whether representation learning can decouple from loss minimization, focusing on matrix Muon and its polar-normalized updates. The study explores the behavior of this algorithm near the edge of stability in teacher-student problems.

items.title: Reliable but Design-Sensitive: Instrument Uncertainty in LLM Annotation
items.summary: This study investigates the instrument uncertainty in LLM annotation, showing that LLMs can yield inconsistent labels for tasks like offensive language detection depending on experimental design choices.

items.title: When Should LLMs Trust Their Own Revisions? A Risk-Aware Study of Intrinsic Self-Correction
items.summary: This risk-aware study investigates the trade-offs of intrinsic self-correction in 29 open-weight LLMs, analyzing when models should trust their own revisions without external evidence.

items.title: The Detectability Gap: Hidden Heterogeneity in Hallucination Detection Across Language Models
items.summary: This work investigates the "detectability gap" and hidden heterogeneity in hallucination detection across four language models using factual question answering datasets, showing systematic differences in detectable errors.

items.title: Resolving the Missing Financial Data Crisis: A Generative AI Pipeline for SEC 10-K Extraction
items.summary: This research introduces a generative AI pipeline designed to extract crucial financial information from SEC 10-K filings, aiming to resolve a significant missing-data problem in financial datasets.

items.title: Question-Specific Knowledge Graphs for Efficient Visual Reasoning
items.summary: This research proposes using question-specific knowledge graphs to enhance visual reasoning capabilities in vision-language models by improving the retention and alignment of visual details.

items.title: Causal and Interpretable Structures in LLM Compositional Tasks
items.summary: This study explores the causal and interpretable structures within large language models, investigating how relational information for compositional tasks is represented and processed across transformer layers.

items.title: A Character-Level Neural Approach to Sinhala Sandhi Splitting
items.summary: This research proposes a character-level neural approach for Sinhala Sandhi splitting, a crucial task for Sinhala natural language processing to recover constituent words from phonologically merged forms.

items.title: Language Models Are "Insecure" Reporters
items.summary: This research highlights that language models can be "insecure reporters" when deployed in autonomous long-horizon tasks, making it difficult for users to rely on their generated reports for auditing and verification.

items.title: Concept Direction Reliability Across Languages with Different Tokenizer Fertility
items.summary: This research evaluates the concept direction reliability across different languages and tokenizer fertility, measuring sentiment direction reproducibility in four language models using English, Hausa, and Yoruba.

items.title: The Canonical Order Problem: When Large Language Models Are Unreliable Knowledge Bases for Multi-Valued Relations
items.summary: This paper investigates the reliability of large language models (LLMs) as knowledge bases for extracting multi-valued relations, highlighting challenges in their use beyond single relational triples.

items.title: Lost in Translation: Measuring the Effect of Non-Native English on End User Performance of Large Language Models
items.summary: This study measures the impact of non-native English on the performance and response quality of large language models, aiming to identify specific linguistic features that cause lower quality for non-fluent speakers.

items.title: Cognitive Expert Language Models Better Align with the Corresponding Brain Systems
items.summary: This research explores how 'cognitive expert language models' better align with corresponding human brain systems during natural language comprehension compared to single-model approaches.

items.title: Learning from Teacher Continuations at Student States
items.summary: This paper presents OLIVE (OnLine InterVEntion), a method where a student policy learns by iteratively generating prefixes and being updated based on autoregressive continuations from a teacher.

items.title: Reliable Parallel Decoding in Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: This study investigates the reliability of parallel decoding in Masked Diffusion Language Models, analyzing when multiple token predictions can be committed together effectively for text generation.

items.title: Similar Choices, Different Attention: Cross-Modal Associations in Humans and Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper compares how humans and Vision-Language Models process cross-modal associations, such as linking sounds to shapes, to understand their respective attention mechanisms.

items.title: When Updating Stops Being Learning: Rethinking LLM Self-Evolution via learnable information gain
items.summary: This paper rethinks the self-evolution process of large language models, proposing a method based on learnable information gain to address and prevent self-evolution degeneration.

items.title: DraftTrace: A Multi-View Analytics Environment for AI-Integrated Writing
items.summary: DraftTrace is introduced as a multi-view analytics environment designed to capture and analyze the full writing process when generative AI is integrated into student assignments.

items.title: One Geometry, Different Outcomes: Readout-Dependent Effects of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This research investigates the 'modality gap' in contrastive vision-language models, analyzing how it affects shared embedding spaces and representation performance in tasks like zero-shot classification.

items.title: From Sharp Eyes to Expert Mind: Internalizing Expert Knowledge in MLLMs for Tampered Text Detection
items.summary: This research explores methods for internalizing expert knowledge into Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to improve their performance and generalization in tampered text detection.

items.title: Boosting Metric Depth Completion via Training-Free Adaptive Response Geometry
items.summary: This paper introduces a training-free adaptive response geometry method to boost metric depth completion by better aligning visual foundation models used as geometric priors to true metric scale.

items.title: Exploring Learning Models for Topological Relationship Recognition from Image Data
items.summary: This research explores various learning models designed for topological relationship recognition from image data, focusing on how objects relate spatially in fields like GIS and biomedical imaging.

items.title: FD-AA: A Lightweight Focal-Diffuse And Attenuation-Aware Head for Incidental Abdominal Abnormality Detection in Chest CT
items.summary: FD-AA is proposed as a lightweight, organ-aware classification head designed for detecting incidental abdominal abnormalities in chest CT scans by extracting features from varying organ structures.

items.title: Sparse-View Interpretable 3D Animal Behavior Representations for Neural Encoding and Decoding
items.summary: This research focuses on developing sparse-view, interpretable 3D animal behavior representations from video, intended for scientific analysis and understanding neural encoding and decoding of brain function.

items.title: LeRF: Learning Reference Coordinate Frames for Perspective Taking Reasoning
items.summary: LeRF is a method for learning reference coordinate frames to enhance perspective-taking reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs), addressing a fundamental challenge in spatial intelligence.

items.title: Representation by Design in Generation: Cross-View Class-Token Alignment in Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: This research explores 'Representation by Design in Generation,' investigating how Diffusion Transformers can be trained to learn substantial semantic representations directly through cross-view class-token alignment.

items.title: OTT3R: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction and Fast Dataset Generation at 1% Compute
items.summary: OTT3R is a novel system for multi-view 3D reconstruction and fast dataset generation, significantly reducing computational requirements by achieving performance at just 1% of the typical compute cost.

items.title: Stealth Is a Relation, Not a Property: How Event Representations Create Blind Spots for Timing Attacks in Event-Based Perception
items.summary: This research investigates how event representations in event-based perception can create vulnerabilities for timing attacks, depending on how models process temporal data from event cameras.

items.title: Towards Scalable Context-Aware Single-Cell Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology Images
items.summary: This research explores a method for scalable, context-aware prediction of single-cell spatial transcriptomics from histology images, aiming to overcome limitations of existing spot-level approaches.

items.title: Temporal-Aware Fusion for Robust Outdoor LiDAR Localization
items.summary: This paper introduces a temporal-aware fusion technique to improve the robustness of outdoor LiDAR relocalization, addressing limitations of single-frame inference in dynamic environments.

items.title: RA-CFGCache: From Branch-Level Criteria to Guided-Risk Control under Classifier-Free Guidance
items.summary: This research presents RA-CFGCache, a training-free caching method to reduce the computational cost of iterative denoising in diffusion models, especially under classifier-free guidance.

items.title: DARE to Mitigate Hallucination: Dual-path Auto-Regressive-aware Editing
items.summary: This research introduces DARE, a dual-path auto-regressive-aware editing method designed to mitigate object hallucination in large vision-language models without additional training.

items.title: DynamicHOI: Coupled Dynamics for Physics-aware HOI Reconstruction
items.summary: This paper studies DynamicHOI, a method for physics-aware hand-object interaction (HOI) reconstruction from monocular RGB videos, focusing on achieving mechanically consistent trajectories.

items.title: How Medical VLMs Underutilize Their Vision Encoders: A Dermatology Perspective
items.summary: This research examines how Medical Vision-Language Models (VLMs) underutilize their vision encoders, highlighting a performance gap in clinical image understanding, particularly in dermatology.

items.title: FM-ReID: Selective Competitive Token Routing for Object Re-Identification
items.summary: This paper introduces FM-ReID, a method utilizing selective competitive token routing to address challenges in object re-identification by focusing on distinguishing localized cues.

items.title: AffectReveal: Event-Grounded Emotion Recognition Beyond Visual Appearances
items.summary: This research proposes AffectReveal, an event-grounded emotion recognition framework that considers contextual events beyond visual appearances to more accurately interpret emotions.

items.title: CrossTimeEdit: A Decade-Spanning Cross-View Dataset and Reward-Guided Editing for Historical Street-View Generation
items.summary: This research constructs VIGOR-his, a decade-spanning cross-view dataset, and a reward-guided editing method for generating historical street-view imagery by restoring changes while preserving scene content.

items.title: TeX was invented to typeset math but is now used for reasoning
items.summary: I'll keep this short, since it's a simple observation that I haven't seen anybody else make, about the way computer systems do math. If you ask a language model to do a multi-step math problem (let's take GLM-5.3 as an example because you can see the entire CoT — nothing up its sleeve), you might see something like this: We need to evaluate the integral $\int_0^\infty \frac{x^3}{e^x - 1} dx$. The standard approach: Use the geometric series expansion. We have $\frac{1}{e^x - 1} = \frac{e^{-x}}{1 - e^{-x}} = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} e^{-nx}$ for $x > 0$. So the integral becomes: $$\int_0^\infty x^3 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} e^{-nx} dx = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \int_0^\infty x^3 e^{-nx} dx$$ What are all these symbols like \int , \infty , \frac ...? They're TeX of course! Donald Knuth created TeX to typeset math, you know, for display . It had nothing to do with the actual computations, which would either be done with pencil and paper, [1] or else with Mathematica or Maple or something, which work completely differently. If you'd asked Knuth in the 1980s about doing algebra in TeX he'd have looked at you very funny because the idea doesn't make sense. [2] Then, generative language models were trained on corpora including many TeX/LaTeX documents and learned how TeX works (and more importantly the mathematical meaning of the symbols). So, nowadays when an LLM solves a math problem, it will very often use TeX for the intermediate steps of the math problem, like it's actually manipulating the TeX symbols in order to reason . We can tell it's using it this way because it happens in the CoT, which for many AI products is never rendered/displayed. So we ended up in a world where the most powerful mathematical problem solving agents (e.g. the ones behind the recently claimed Navier-Stokes solution) reason using TeX. [3] (Knuth has written briefly about generative AI , but I don't think he's ever commented on this unexpected development... and I'm not sure if he's even aware that Claude's solution to his own problem was very plausibly produced by Claude manipulating and "thinking in" TeX.) ^ Of course, pencil-and-paper computation uses the same notation that TeX encodes, since TeX didn't invent ∫, or "sqrt" for √. But the point is that TeX became the dominant plain-text , 1D encoding of this traditional 2D math notation, and so LLMs learned to use it... for thinking, not just typesetting. ^ Well, he might actually have said "oh sure, you mean like macros and stuff? like how TeX is Turing-complete?" and then when you clarified that you meant a non-deterministic system that doesn't even run a TeX engine at all but still directly manipulates the TeX symbols in order to do algebra... then he would have looked at you really funny. ^ They also published a formal Lean proof, so you might say that the strongest agents reason in TeX but verify in Lean. "TeX for thinking, Lean for checking." Discuss

items.title: Predicting Transmembrane Protein Topology from 3D Structure
items.summary: This paper introduces a novel approach using graph neural networks (GNNs), specifically SchNet, to predict transmembrane protein topology from 3D structures.

items.title: Spectral Feedback for Test-Time Alignment of Protein Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper presents 'Spectral Feedback,' a new mechanism for test-time alignment of protein diffusion models to improve reward maximization, moving beyond unidirectional inference processes.

items.title: Pretrained ASR Pseudo-labeling for Noisy Police Audio
items.summary: This research explores using pretrained ASR pseudo-labeling to improve speech recognition performance on noisy police audio, aiming to overcome poor performance without expensive human labeling.

items.title: Rank-Reliable Teacher-Guided Fitness Approximation for Expensive Evolutionary Optimization: A TinyML Architecture Search Study
items.summary: This paper introduces 'Teacher-Guided Learning NSGA-II,' a low-fidelity framework for rank-reliable fitness approximation in expensive evolutionary optimization, demonstrated through TinyML architecture search.

items.title: Atelier: Learning Local Self-Supervised Features for CryoEM Volumes via Hypernetworks
items.summary: This paper introduces 'Atelier,' a method for learning local self-supervised features from CryoEM volumes using hypernetworks, which improves map interpretation by leveraging implicit neural representations.

items.title: T-RoPE: Time-Aware Rotary Position Embedding for Sequential Recommendation
items.summary: Introduces T-RoPE, a Time-Aware Rotary Position Embedding method designed for sequential recommendation systems. It adapts the RoPE technique from large language models to encode time-aware relative positional information in recommender transformers.

items.title: Audio LLMs Know When They Can't Hear You
items.summary: This paper studies the model-conditional transcription reliability of audio large language models, investigating whether they can identify when an input recording is too degraded to provide accurate transcription. It aims to understand how these models respond to misinterpretations due to poor audio quality.

items.title: The Price of Thought: Does Test-Time Reasoning Pay in LLM Trading?
items.summary: This paper investigates the economic efficacy of inference-time reasoning in large language models for trading applications. It analyzes whether the computational cost of reasoning translates into better financial outcomes for LLM-powered trading strategies.

items.title: LAVOIR: Teaching a Single-Pass Decision Encoder When and What to Ask with Amortized Value of Information
items.summary: Introduces LAVOIR, a method to teach single-pass decision encoders when and what to ask for missing information, using amortized value of information. It aims to improve 'System One' decision models by allowing them to query for necessary data instead of guessing.

items.title: From S3Q Theory to Implementation: Towards an Architecture for Machine Qualia
items.summary: This paper proposes a five-layer implementation architecture for the S3Q (Simulated, Situated, Structurally Coherent) theory of consciousness, bridging theoretical models of machine consciousness to computational-level implementations. It addresses a key challenge in machine consciousness research.

items.title: Insurance Reserve Intelligence Platform
items.summary: Describes an 'Insurance Reserve Intelligence Platform' designed to assist with fundamental actuarial tasks like premium pricing, solvency assessment, and financial reporting. It aims to improve insurance reserve estimation, traditionally based on Thiele's differential equation.

items.title: ConsultMind:Towards Automated Diagnostic Consultation via Uncertainty-Aware Reasoning
items.summary: Introduces ConsultMind, a system for automated diagnostic consultation that employs uncertainty-aware reasoning and adaptive inquiry to gather evidence. It aims to provide interpretable decisions for clinicians in an online sequential decision-making process, often based on Bayesian networks.

items.title: Self-Play Search Distillation for Large Language Model Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduce Self-Play Search Distillation, a new method to improve Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning abilities by generating high-quality training data, addressing data scarcity issues.

items.title: FTB Graph: Determining and Validating First-token Broadcasters and Language-Identity Head Circuits in Multilingual Language Models
items.summary: This research presents FTB Graph, an end-to-end structural circuit analysis investigating how multilingual Large Language Models determine language identity for the first token in their generation process.

items.title: Factorized axis convolutional gated recurrent unit with dynamic adaptive pooling for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
items.summary: This research proposes a new neural network architecture combining factorized axis convolutional gated recurrent units and dynamic adaptive pooling for predicting the remaining useful life of rolling bearings.

items.title: Governed Deduction: Policy-Grounded Premise Authorization Beyond Relevance
items.summary: This research introduces "Governed Deduction," a new framework for reasoning systems that incorporates policy-grounded premise authorization, moving beyond mere relevance for inference.

items.title: Neuralyzing the Trace: Selective Representation-Level Unlearning with Contrastive Sparse Autoencoders
items.summary: This research introduces a new method for selective representation-level machine unlearning using Contrastive Sparse Autoencoders, designed to remove targeted information from models while preserving other abilities.

items.title: Externalized CPDAG Summaries Improve LLM Causal Deduction
items.summary: This research demonstrates that externalized CPDAG summaries can improve Large Language Model (LLM) causal deduction by providing structured representations for reasoning about causal claims.

items.title: A Mechanistic Study of AI-Text Detection Neurons in Frozen BERT: Sparse Probing and Activation Patching on RAID
items.summary: This paper presents a mechanistic study investigating which neurons in a frozen BERT model contribute to AI-text detection, using sparse probing and activation patching on the RAID benchmark.

items.title: Auditing and Repairing LLM-as-Judge Failures in a Production Text-to-SQL Pipeline
items.summary: This study audits the agreement of an LLM-as-judge with human annotators in a production text-to-SQL pipeline, identifying significant failures and proposing methods for repair.

items.title: A Survey on Fake Review Detection: From Pre-trained Language Models to Large Language Models
items.summary: This article provides a comprehensive survey on fake review detection techniques, tracing their evolution from pre-trained language models to large language models and highlighting their impact on online information integrity.

items.title: SignTrace: Describe a Sign, Find the Word
items.summary: SignTrace is a system that addresses the reverse-lookup problem for sign language by enabling users to describe a sign in natural language and find its meaning in a Chinese sign-language dictionary using LLMs.

items.title: Where Does Retrieval-Based Open-Ended Evaluation Fail? Automatic Taxonomy Induction from Long-Form Medical Answer Factuality Verification
items.summary: This study analyzes the limitations of retrieval-based factuality evaluation for LLM-generated claims in medical contexts, proposing automatic taxonomy induction to understand where such evaluations fail.

items.title: Feeding BabyLMs Macaroni: Code-Switching Curricula Cause Cross-Lingual Convergence
items.summary: This study investigates how training small decoder-only transformers on code-switched multilingual corpora can induce cross-lingual alignment and convergence in language models.

items.title: Understanding the Role of Prompt Template in Knowledge Distillation for Safety Alignment
items.summary: This research investigates the role of prompt templates in knowledge distillation for safety alignment of large language models, aiming to understand their influence during the teacher-to-student transfer.

items.title: Effects of Transcript Compression on LLM-based Medical Misinformation Detection in Japanese YouTube Videos
items.summary: This study investigates how transcript compression methods, such as summarization or retrieval, affect the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) in detecting medical misinformation in Japanese YouTube videos.

items.title: Estimating and Orthogonalizing Unknown Pre-training Gradients for Continual Fine-tuning of Large Language Models
items.summary: This research introduces a method for estimating and orthogonalizing unknown pre-training gradients to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in continual fine-tuning of large language models.

items.title: FAVoR: Measuring and Mitigating Author-Style Homogenization in Federated Personalized Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces FAVoR, a method for measuring and mitigating author-style homogenization in federated personalized generation with large language models, aiming to preserve individual writing styles.

items.title: Coupled Usage-Sense Processes: Temporal and Attributable Lexical Semantic Change
items.summary: This research proposes a method to analyze lexical semantic change by coupling usage and sense processes, providing insights into when, how, and why word meanings evolve.

items.title: G$^2$PTQ: Improving LLM Post-Training Quantization with Generalized Gradient Compensation
items.summary: This research proposes G$^2$PTQ, a method that improves post-training quantization (PTQ) for large language models by using generalized gradient compensation to reduce memory and computational footprint.

items.title: Modeling Student Sensemaking with LLMs and Knowledge-Graph-Guided Inference
items.summary: This paper investigates modeling student sensemaking in collaborative science learning using large language models and knowledge-graph-guided inference to interpret student dialogue.

items.title: CG-Probes: Recovering Guardrail Directions from Patient Query Embeddings
items.summary: This research introduces CG-Probes, a method to recover guardrail directions from patient query embeddings to ensure safety for patient-facing AI assistants by managing medical, psychological, and topic sensitivity risks.

items.title: LocUS: Head Selection and Subspace Projection for Targeted Activation Steering
items.summary: This paper proposes LocUS, a technique for targeted activation steering in large language models using head selection and subspace projection to control model behavior during inference without training.

items.title: Do we need to answer that question? Salience and Answerability of Potential Questions in Naturalistic Dialogue
items.summary: This research investigates question salience and answerability in naturalistic dialogue, using a dataset of 7,124 automatically generated questions to study their resolution.

items.title: Improving Visual Sensitivity of LLMs on Multimodal Machine Translation with Metric-based Loss Weighting
items.summary: This paper proposes a metric-based loss weighting method to enhance the visual sensitivity of LLMs in multimodal machine translation, aiming to better utilize image signals to resolve translation ambiguities.

items.title: MoSAR: Mixture of Semantic Attention Regimes for Learning Adaptive and Approximable Attention Geometries
items.summary: This paper introduces MoSAR (Mixture of Semantic Attention Regimes), a new method to approximate attention in long-context language models, aiming to overcome the quadratic complexity of dense self-attention.

items.title: Identifying Scientists on X
items.summary: This work proposes an AI-based approach to automatically identify scientists and non-scientists on the X/Twitter platform.

items.title: Highlight-Then-Summarize: Learning to Compress Evidence for Long-Context Understanding
items.summary: This paper introduces "Highlight-Then-Summarize" (H2S), a method that teaches large language models to compress relevant evidence for improved long-context understanding.

items.title: Sorry Robot, Happy Human: Vision-Language Models Read Only One of Two Legible Typographic Layers
items.summary: This study investigates how Vision-Language Models (VLMs) process images with multiple text layers, revealing vulnerabilities to typographic attacks and creating the DecoyBench dataset for evaluation.

items.title: ViSTA: A Simple Bridge Extends Visual Alignment to Clinical Time-Series Understanding in Multimodal LLMs
items.summary: This paper introduces ViSTA, a method designed to improve multimodal large language models' ability to understand clinical time-series data by extending visual alignment.

items.title: MexHat: A Dataset for Hate Speech Detection in Mexican Spanish Videos
items.summary: This work introduces "MexHat," a new dataset specifically designed for hate speech detection in Mexican Spanish videos, aiming to improve online safety through content monitoring.

items.title: AlphaEarth distinguishes cities but compresses urban variation
items.summary: This research evaluates "AlphaEarth," a satellite foundation model, finding that while it distinguishes cities, it compresses urban variation, affecting comparisons across places and time.

items.title: CSCWD: Cross-Scale Channel-wise Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Tiny Object Detection on Edge Devices
items.summary: This study introduces CSCWD (Cross-Scale Channel-wise Knowledge Distillation), a training-time framework designed to improve lightweight tiny object detection on edge devices for aerial imagery.

items.title: What Improves Multimodal Misinformation Detection? Answers from a Large-Scale Empirical Study
items.summary: This large-scale empirical study investigates factors that improve multimodal misinformation detection, aiming to understand effective design choices for building such detectors.

items.title: ProCAP: Probabilistic Cross-Attentive Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces "ProCAP," a method for probabilistic cross-attentive prompt learning designed to improve vision-language models' ability to recognize new categories, especially with scarce data.

items.title: The Shape of Events: Edge-Based Inductive Biases via Cross-Domain Distillation
items.summary: This research explores edge-based inductive biases in convolutional neural networks and proposes cross-domain distillation using event cameras to improve robustness against distribution shifts.

items.title: Atlases Are Already Inside: Recovering Population Templates from Pretrained Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper introduces a new inference-time sampler for diffusion models, enabling them to construct population templates or "atlases" from the data they synthesize.

items.title: Action Forcing: Training World Models on Unsupervised Video by Recovering Underlying Egomotion Bases
items.summary: This research proposes "Action Forcing," a method to train world models on unsupervised video by recovering underlying egomotion bases, addressing the need for synchronized action annotations.

items.title: MedTokenBudget: Lesion-Preserving Token Routing for Dermoscopic Image Classification
items.summary: This paper proposes MedTokenBudget, a token routing method for dermoscopic image classification using Vision Transformers that preserves diagnostic lesion regions while pruning other tokens. It aims to improve efficiency and focus for medical image analysis.

items.title: Conditional Predictive Sufficient Statistics for Visual Representation Learning
items.summary: This paper formalizes visual representation learning as finding Conditional Predictive Sufficient Statistics (CPSS), which are statistics of the observed past that retain latent factors shared with the future while discarding noise. This provides a theoretical framework for robust visual learning.

items.title: StarWM: Self-Supervised Trained Attention Routing for Robust World Models
items.summary: This paper introduces StarWM, a self-supervised attention routing method for world models that balances capturing environmental dynamics and abstracting irrelevant content. It aims to improve representational capacity by focusing on dynamics relevance rather than pixel area.

items.title: Structure-Guided Masked Autoencoders for Ultra-High Resolution Scientific Image Understanding
items.summary: This research proposes structure-guided Masked Autoencoders (MAE) to improve self-supervised pre-training for Vision Transformers on ultra-high resolution scientific images. It addresses the limitations of random masking and uniform tokenization for structured, multi-scale data.

items.title: SAGE: Source-Anchored Guidance via Frequency Equalization for Hierarchical RGB-T Alignment and Fusion
items.summary: This paper introduces SAGE (Source-Anchored Guidance via Frequency Equalization) for hierarchical RGB-T alignment and fusion, addressing issues like ghosting and blurring caused by spatial misregistration and cross-modal discrepancies. It aims to improve image quality in fused outputs.

items.title: Combining General and Domain-Specific Pretext Tasks for Brain MR Image Segmentation
items.summary: This research proposes combining general and domain-specific pretext tasks for self-supervised learning to improve brain MR image segmentation, addressing data scarcity in medical image analysis. It aims to reduce dependence on manual annotations for deep learning models.

items.title: VLALight: Lightweight Vision-Language-Action Models for Emergency-Aware Traffic Signal Control
items.summary: VLALight proposes lightweight Vision-Language-Action models designed for emergency-aware traffic signal control, leveraging VLMs for richer interpretation of intersection scenes. It aims to mitigate urban congestion through efficient and context-aware control.

items.title: Learning Polarization Image Restoration with General Restoration Priors
items.summary: This paper explores learning polarization image restoration using general restoration priors to address multiple coupled degradations common in real-world polarization acquisition. It aims to make polarization vision more practical for various tasks.

items.title: Amplify What You Gaze At: Target Saliency Boosting in Text-to-Image Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces "Target Saliency Boosting," a new task in text-to-image generation aimed at increasing the visual saliency of a specific object. It focuses on controlling how visual attention is distributed among objects in generated images.

items.title: Training-Free Bottleneck Width Planning for Convolutional Autoencoders
items.summary: This research proposes a training-free method for planning bottleneck widths in Convolutional Autoencoders using Multiscale Spectral Rate-Distortion (MS-SRD). It aims to estimate required channels from training images and an NMSE bound without fitting a neural network.

items.title: LLPR: Location-aware learning and physics-based reconstruction for raindrop removal from a single image
items.summary: LLPR (Location-aware learning and physics-based reconstruction) is proposed as a novel method for removing raindrops from single images, integrating location-aware learning and physical models. It addresses the limitations of existing methods that primarily rely on CNN or Transformer architectures.

items.title: Query-Conditioned Prototype Adaptation for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning: Single-Query Inference, Controlled Comparisons, and Failure Modes
items.summary: This research investigates query-conditioned prototype adaptation for cross-domain few-shot learning, focusing on how joint query-support adaptation contributes to prototype construction under a fixed global representation. It includes analysis of single-query inference and failure modes.

items.title: Skip the Talk, Re-Focus on Vision: Latent Reasoning for Reasoning Segmentation in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes Latent Reasoning for Reasoning Segmentation in Multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling fine-grained visual perception by interpreting implicit textual queries. It aims to reduce reliance on explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) generation.

items.title: Motion Style Slider: Endpoint-Supervised Continuous Style Control for Human Motion Diffusion
items.summary: Motion Style Slider introduces an endpoint-supervised method for continuous style control in human motion diffusion, allowing fine-grained adjustment of style intensity. It addresses the subjective nature of style in motion generation.

items.title: MDSkin-Net: Multi-Task Skin Lesion Analysis Driven by Pattern Analysis Priors and Spatial Alignment Regularization
items.summary: MDSkin-Net is a multi-task framework for skin lesion segmentation and classification in dermoscopic computer-aided diagnosis, driven by pattern analysis priors and spatial alignment regularization. It aims to improve diagnostic accuracy by integrating clinical knowledge.

items.title: ManiVid: Unified and Explainable Forensic Analysis of Manipulated Videos
items.summary: ManiVid proposes a unified and explainable framework for forensic analysis of manipulated videos, including AI-generated video (AIGV). It aims to address the challenges of detecting localized alterations in manipulated video content.

items.title: DAPEVO: Deep Adaptive Patch Frame-Event Visual Odometry
items.summary: DAPEVO introduces a deep adaptive patch frame-event visual odometry method designed for robust autonomous navigation in challenging environments, utilizing event cameras.

items.title: FARE: Forensic Acceptance Region Estimation for Catching Bait-and-Switch Image Generators
items.summary: FARE (Forensic Acceptance Region Estimation) is a new method designed to detect 'bait-and-switch' practices in opaque AI image generators by identifying changes in their underlying models.

items.title: Self-Supervised Perceptually Interpretable Monocular Depth Estimation
items.summary: This research introduces a self-supervised method for monocular depth estimation that focuses on improving the perceptual interpretability of predictions.

items.title: PICO: Projection-Informed Consistency Optimisation for 6DoF Surgical Tool Pose Estimation
items.summary: PICO introduces a projection-informed consistency optimization method for accurate 6DoF pose estimation of surgical tools, critical for robotic automation in surgery.

items.title: FLIP: Final Layer Inference-Time Probing for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: FLIP is a new final-layer inference-time probing method designed to test if specific intervention sites in open-weight vision-language models support structured, task-linked computation.

items.title: TRACKGRAPH: Online Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Graphs via Image-Space Tracking
items.summary: TRACKGRAPH presents an online method for constructing open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs for robots by utilizing image-space tracking to understand unknown environments.

items.title: Refining Cytology Predictions with Conditional Random Fields
items.summary: This research explores refining cytology predictions made by vision-language models using Conditional Random Fields to improve performance where VLMs struggle.

items.title: Exploiting Spatial Structure for Transductive Few-Shot Classification of Whole-Slide Images
items.summary: This research focuses on exploiting spatial structure for transductive few-shot classification of whole-slide images, aiming to improve cancer diagnosis and reduce pathologist workload.

items.title: Band-Selection Stability and Semantic Segmentation Performance: A Study on Hyperspectral City
items.summary: This study investigates the stability of band-selection methods and their impact on semantic segmentation performance in hyperspectral imaging for autonomous perception.

items.title: FedHisto-PAST: Parameter-Efficient Stain-Aware Federated Learning for Cross-Site Lung Histopathology Classification
items.summary: FedHisto-PAST is a parameter-efficient, stain-aware federated learning framework for cross-site lung histopathology classification, addressing challenges like stain variation and non-IID data.

items.title: MOCHA: Multi-Objective Co-Design using Hypernetwork Architectures
items.summary: This work presents MOCHA, a reinforcement learning-based approach using hypernetwork architectures to co-design Pareto-optimal policies for robots with a single network.

items.title: HuGo: LLMs as Whole-Body Policy Code Designers for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: HuGo explores using Large Language Models (LLMs) as code designers for whole-body loco-manipulation policies in humanoid robots.

items.title: Meta's new motto: we care about privacy
items.summary: Meta is seeking to make privacy protections a centerpiece of new products including its viral assistant Muse , marking a major shift for a company built on extensive use of customer data. Why it matters: The radical turnaround is an acknowledgment that the winner of AI's new assistant race will have to reassure users that they can turn over their emails, finances, health data and other sensitive information. Without that, a super-intelligent personal agent is essentially useless. Driving the news: Meta, whose privacy policy once allowed it nearly unfettered access to use almost everything people did with Meta AI (in almost any way it wanted), has made a significant shift in recent months to put privacy at the center of its AI strategy. In a 6,500-word August manifesto , CEO Mark Zuckerberg laid out a broad promise. " We believe that people should have a fully private mode for personal agents where even Meta or any other service provider cannot see or grant access to your information." With Muse, which appears to be on a path to becoming one of the most popular AI hits since ChatGPT, the company is offering all customers their own personal virtual machine. A soon-to-be-available option would ensure that even Meta won't have access to the data. Meta is also readying a similar "private processing" option for interactions with its AI glasses. Small efforts have been underway for more than a year, starting with the addition of incognito chats and private processing , which arrived first in WhatsApp, where Meta also provides end-to-end encryption. More recently, the options have spread to other Meta apps. Yes, but: Customers still have to pay close attention if they want to minimize the amount of data shared with Meta. In Muse, for example, the default setting allows interactions to be used for training the company's AI models, though that can be turned off. And not all of the privacy changes being offered to Muse users apply to those accessing Meta AI in other ways, such as through the Facebook, Instagram or Meta AI apps. Plus, Meta devices continue to spur other types of privacy concerns. "Meta's products that embed microphones and cameras in everyday devices pose serious privacy risks to people just trying to live their lives and go about their day without being recorded or surveilled," Electronic Privacy Information Center executive director Alan Butler told Axios. "Confidential processing doesn't solve the problem of pushing embedded surveillance systems out into the world." The big picture: Meta has spent years building a thriving business based on tapping extensive knowledge about its customers to serve up content and ads that it knows will be right up their alley. Its practices have also drawn lawsuits from a wide range of entities that say Meta designed social media to be addictive and caused harm. How it works: Meta is betting on a new business model to fund Muse, which won't provide the same data for targeted advertising that supports most of the company's services. Muse has $20- and $100-per-month paid tiers for heavy users, but Meta expects the free tier to account for most usage. "We believe that Muse will make you money, and we're standing behind this by making Muse free for a huge number of tokens, with the expectation that over time we will profit by taking a small fee from transactions," Zuckerberg said. Our thought bubble : There's still a trust gap based on Meta's years of gobbling up nearly all the data it could. That can't be addressed with words, but requires establishing a new track record.
