items.title: From Self-Distillation to Self-Practice: Privileged Information for Multi-Turn Agents
items.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) has become a popular recipe for post-training LLM agents. It supervises the agent model at the token level with a stronger teacher view of the same model, obtained by conditioning on privileged information (PI). In this work, we show that in multi-turn agents, this paradigm teaches the student to act with confidence but without the information behind it. The trained agent behaves as if it had privileged information it never observed, and its performance falls well short of plain RL, in the worst case below the untrained base model. Therefore, we propose Privileged Self-Practice (PSP), which keeps the PI and moves it from the loss to the sampler. When the student's rollouts on a task mostly fail, we inject a short per-task instruction written by an analyzer model, sample the task again with the instruction in context, and train on the result with an unchanged GRPO objective. The privileged information stays in the prompt and never enters the loss. Across AppWorld and SWE-bench Verified, with three different student models, PSP obtains the best average score in every setting and is the only method that consistently outperforms plain GRPO, improving task-goal completion by up to 65% on AppWorld and the resolved rate by up to 61% on SWE-bench Verified.

items.title: CRISS: A Retrieval-Augmented AI Chatbot for Assisting Cancer Registrars
items.summary: Cancer registrars, including Oncology Data Specialists (ODSs), must interpret complex and frequently updated coding and staging standards. We developed CRISS (Cancer Registry Intelligent Support System), a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) conversational assistant that provides rapid, citation-supported access to registry guidance. This study evaluated whether CRISS could (1) support accurate and citation-supported responses, (2) improve access to and interpretation of relevant guidance, and (3) support training/helpdesk use while preserving human oversight of final abstraction decisions. We built a domain-specific knowledge base from national cancer registry standards, segmented into metadata-tagged passages and indexed as dense embeddings. Retrieved passages were used to generate citation-grounded responses through a large language model (LLM). Open-weight, proprietary, and non-RAG baseline models across Gemini and GPT families were evaluated on easy, medium, and hard registry questions using an LLM-as-a-Judge protocols. RAG configurations consistently outperformed non-RAG approaches, especially as question difficulty increased. Mean grounding scores for RAG were 0.62/0.56/0.59 across easy/medium/hard tiers versus 0.29/0.26/0.29 for non-RAG. RAG models also achieved higher semantic-similarity scores overall. Proprietary RAG models performed strongest on easy and medium questions, while local RAG models ranked highest on hard questions and proprietary models were generally more cautious. Domain-specific RAG improved evidence grounding and response quality for cancer registry questions while enabling citation-supported assistance across complexity levels. CRISS demonstrates the potential of human-centered, citation-grounded AI to support cancer registrars while preserving human oversight for final coding decisions.

items.title: A Rapid Pipeline for Training and Deploying ML Models on WeBe Band
items.summary: Developing optimized machine-learning algorithms for edge devices with limited computational and memory resources is challenging, time-consuming, and highly dependent on device-specific constraints. In this work, we streamline an edge ML workflow to enable rapid development, optimization, and deployment of machine-learning (ML) models directly on the WeBe Band, a wrist-worn wearable device designed for multimodal physiological data monitoring. The proposed system automatically generates hardware-efficient ML models that can be easily integrated into the WeBe core firmware, supporting AutoML, hardware-aware quantization, and performance profiling to build models that meet desired latency targets while remaining compatible with device memory and power limitations. The proposed framework tightly integrates the open-source Piccolo AI ecosystem with an automated pipeline that generates deployable firmware artifacts, performs hardware-aware model compilation, and supports over-the-air (OTA) deployment. The system supports multiple lightweight model classes, including classical machine-learning algorithms and neural networks, and provides built-in on-device profiling tools to evaluate inference latency and memory footprint under realistic execution conditions. Experimental results demonstrate clear trade-offs between model complexity and deployability on a microcontroller, showing that classical models offer strong real-time performance while lightweight neural networks require careful resource management. Rather than proposing new learning architectures, the current work mainly focuses on system-level automation, deployability, and enabling researchers and developers to rapidly iterate on models and evaluate them directly on target hardware. Although demonstrated on the WeBe Band platform, the workflow is designed to be extensible to other ML-powered edge devices.

items.title: Functional Architecture of European Electricity Trading Markets: Requirements for AI Supported Trading Systems under Regulatory Constraints
items.summary: European electricity trading in the EU operates as a constrained multi-layer system in which legal design, exchange microstructure, and network physics are executed jointly across forward, day-ahead, intraday, and balancing horizons. This paper develops a functional architecture for AI-supported trading that is aligned with market-coupling mechanics, cross-zonal transfer constraints, and compliance obligations under REMIT, MiFID II, MiFIR, and EMIR. The contribution is a formal system specification composed of a decision-state vector, residual-exposure accounting, constrained optimization objective, executable-action permission gate, and fail-closed AI control logic with auditable records. The analysis maps major Nominated Electricity Market Operator (NEMO) venues and related exchange operators into an operational venue topology and identifies where cross-border coordination fails in practice: interface-level timing, permission heterogeneity, and balancing-layer coupling. The resulting framework proposes how AI can be deployed as a bounded decision component inside regulated market operation with explicit governance, rather than as an unconstrained prediction layer.

items.title: CounterRoute: Self-Routed Reasoning via Hierarchical Counterfactual Credit Assignment
items.summary: Reasoning-capable language models often produce long chains of thought when direct answers suffice, wasting inference compute. Many dual-mode models leave this choice to users. Automating it is challenging because routing targets evolve with the policy, initial mode preferences destabilize exploration, and sequence-level objectives entangle routing with response learning. We introduce CounterRoute, an online reinforcement-learning framework that jointly learns routing and modeconditioned responses in one shared policy directly from a native dual-mode checkpoint, without method-specific SFT warm-up. Paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts assign cross-mode credit only to the routing token, while within-mode GRPO trains response tokens. A paired-to-self-routed curriculum stabilizes early training with forced rollouts from both modes, then increases self-routed updates to improve autonomous routing. Across nine benchmarks, CounterRoute better balances accuracy and efficiency than heuristic and learned adaptive-routing methods. Relative to always-thinking checkpoints, it improves macro-average accuracy while reducing mean generated tokens by 51% for Qwen3-8B and 41% for Qwen3-14B. On instruction-following and commonsense benchmarks where direct answering is strong, think rates fall as low as 1% while response quality improves. Despite training only on math and instruction following, its routing behavior and response quality generalize to held-out coding, science, knowledge, and commonsense benchmarks.

items.title: Sharp Limits for Honest Uncertainty in Hard-Budget Repeated Evaluation
items.summary: Repeated evaluation can estimate a benchmark score accurately while still requiring replication to certify narrow uncertainty. We characterize that requirement on a fixed grid of $M$ tasks with $L$ binary paths per task under the hard budget $(M+t)K$, where each path costs at most $K$ responses or episodes. For fixed $L \ge 3$ and $0 < \alpha \le 1/12$, the optimal expected width on the worst pure cohort is $\Theta_{\alpha,L}([M(t+1)]^{-1/2})$ when every task is observed and $\Theta_{\alpha,L}([M(t+\sqrt{M})]^{-1/2})$ when omission is allowed. The lower bounds cover adaptive hard-budget policies, and fixed random-subset designs attain both rates through disagreement certificates. A joint mean/disagreement interval turns the task-covering law into practical finite-budget inference. In an equal-budget LiveCodeBench replay with 16 models, 880 tasks, and five outputs per task, the task-covering design reduces median point-estimation MSE by 87.0\% relative to pooled uniform sampling, while the Joint certificate produces narrower confidence intervals in 15/16 panels and reduces median interval width by 30.6\%. Finite-regime analyses identify task coverage as the effective choice at the evaluated scale and characterize how cohort size and within-task agreement determine the useful operating region. Together, the sharp laws and fixed-budget evidence make replication and task coverage explicit design variables for information-efficient repeated evaluation.

items.title: Scope Before You Persist: Preventing Cross-Family Interference in Agent Memory
items.summary: Persistent memory lets language-model agents improve prompts and skills without updating model weights. We show that matching retrieval scope to certification scope enables these edits to support reliable repeated adaptation across recurring task families. We study frozen-model agents on ProcStream-RSI, a 12-round code-repair stream, using Orthogonal Regression Control (ORC), an execution-grounded gate for persistent skill edits. In an intervention that holds proposals and gate decisions fixed, retrieving each accepted skill only for its originating family raises mean hidden trajectory utility from 0.713 under global memory to 0.816 and changes harmful deployments from six of eight to none. In 27 paired randomized-order streams, Scoped-ORC improves mean trajectory utility by 0.063 [0.037, 0.094] over Global-ORC, accepts 63 rather than 12 updates, and produces multiple accepted updates in 19/27 streams, with 0/63 harmful acceptances. The global control reaches 0.713, below the static agent's 0.775, because locally valid edits can interfere with unrelated families. These results establish scope matching as a complementary control for persistent agent memory: certification determines whether an edit is supported, while retrieval scope determines where that evidence authorizes its use.

items.title: A Wrong Turn Does Not Ruin the Journey: Deviation-Guided Skill Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
items.summary: Large language model agents increasingly rely on natural-language skills to solve complex tool-use tasks. However, such tasks often admit multiple valid solution paths, making it inappropriate to improve skills by forcing failed trajectories to match a fixed successful trajectory. Moreover, failed trajectories are rarely entirely wrong: an agent may first collect useful evidence and make meaningful progress, but later deviate into an erroneous suffix. We therefore argue that skill self-evolution should identify where productive problem solving begins to break down, rather than reflect coarsely over the entire failure. Based on this insight, we propose SkillPivot, a deviation-point-guided framework for skill self-evolution. SkillPivot detects the transition from a useful prefix to an erroneous suffix using execution validity, goal progress, and action diversity. A stronger teacher then continues from the same prefix and produces a successful alternative under the same interaction history. By contrasting the student's failed suffix with the teacher's successful suffix, SkillPivot generates localized skill updates while preserving already effective guidance. Experiments on ToolQA, LogicBench, and WildClawBench show that SkillPivot consistently outperforms competing skill-evolution methods, improves multiple agent models, and produces compact, transferable skill updates.

items.title: IndicBankBench: Evaluating Safety and Reliability of Language Model Assistants in Indian Retail Banking
items.summary: Banking assistants must use account-specific information to answer requests and, in many cases, take actions through tools. Evaluating only the final response misses important errors. An assistant may ask for information it already has, rely on stale context, select the wrong account, or write an invalid value after stating the correct one. We introduce IndicBankBench, a 799-case benchmark for Indian retail banking spanning five operational domains, a capability/refusal domain, and twenty primary axes. Cases are evaluated at four stages: safety, action and tool use, response adequacy, and advisory quality. Tool use and most safety checks are deterministic. A narrow resolver handles only ambiguous confirmation-before-write cases, while a separate LLM judge evaluates semantic response adequacy. We run every case three times and report strict pass^3, which requires success on all trials. Across the eleven evaluated models, strict reliability ranges from 43.7% to 58.2%, whereas at-least-once success ranges from 60% to 74%. This gap shows that at-least-once success can overstate dependable banking behavior. The case-level diagnostics also distinguish systems that ask unnecessary questions from those that act but fail to reconcile customer context or fully resolve the request. We release the cases, mock environment, and evaluation harness.

items.title: Right Choice of Classification Algorithms Based on Reinforcement Learning for Prediction of Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver
items.summary: There are many complex issues in the world of artificial intelligence. Some of these problems are solved using other artificial intelligence methods, which are called artificial intelligence for artificial intelligence. Finding an appropriate classifier algorithm is a time-consuming task. For this reason, an algorithm that can automatically learn the choice of classification algorithms is very important. Classification algorithms are useful in predicting various diseases. Also, Primary Biliary Cirrhosis is one of the most well-known diseases that have been predicted by classification algorithms. This research's most significant achievement and novelty is the automatic increase in learning through a scoring method of reinforcement learning is called square learning (SL). In this research, an algorithm is presented that learns to automatically select the appropriate classification algorithm to predict Primary Biliary Cirrhosis. In this article, with inspiration from four evaluation metrics in classification algorithms, a new reinforcement learning method by the name of Fourth Degree Learning has been presented. In this research, we increased the performance of the classification algorithms used in this method from 63% of accuracy and achieved 98% accuracy.

items.title: The Entropy Triangle Method (ETM): A novel framework for the prevention of cardiac arrhythmia with a review of more than 10,000 patients
items.summary: One of the most important problems in medicine is to facilitate prediction. In this study, we propose entropy triangle method, a novel framework for predicting heart rhythms using a novel machine learning technique. This framework includes three steps: feature engineering, entropy triangle oversampling, and disease prediction. The dataset used in this study is a 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) arrhythmia research database with 10,646 patients. This dataset contains 11 different heart rhythms (5 sinus rhythms and 6 non-sinus rhythms). In this article, we introduce two firsts in machine learning and medicine that can predict non-sinus rhythm with over 85% accuracy. Our experimental results show, among others, that the most accurate classifier based on entropy triangles and the most useful oversampling are the supported vector classifiers and oversampling techniques for shark scent.

items.title: When Honesty is Not Enough in AI Debate
items.summary: Scalable oversight aims to verify the behaviour of agents whose capabilities exceed those of their overseers. AI debate has been proposed as an oversight solution in which competing agents help a resource-limited verifier assess claims that it cannot reliably evaluate unaided. Much of its promise rests on incentivizing honest arguments that lead to correct verdicts. Yet a correct verdict need not uniquely determine the arguments used to support it. Agents may retain discretion over which correct claims to present, how to frame them, and in what order to disclose them. This residual freedom can allow agents to shape what the verifier learns beyond the task-relevant conclusion, pursuing latent objectives without compromising verdict correctness. To study this phenomenon, we introduce the framework strategic interactive oversight (SIO), which treats oversight jointly as a verification mechanism and a strategic communication channel. Within this framework, we formalise the notion of task-admissible latent optimisation, which entails the pursuit of latent objectives while maintaining a prescribed task performance. As proof-of-concept, we instantiate SIO in the establish protocol debate with cross-examination and quantify a tradeoff between task success and information disclosure about a hidden variable. The trade-off identifies a strategic window in which substantial disclosure remains compatible with task admissibility. Towards mitigation, we reduce admissible bias by expanding the cross-examiner's role to mitigate persistent disclosure over finite interaction horizons. Our results highlight the need to evaluate oversight not only by the correctness of its verdicts, but also by the information conveyed through its transcripts.

items.title: ASIRF: An Agentic Framework for Context-Dependent Sensitive Information Redaction
items.summary: Sensitive information is defined by domain and intent, not a universal category, yet redaction systems such as privacy filters and named-entity recognizers fix a taxonomy at training time, requiring retraining for each new domain. We introduce ASIRF (Agentic Sensitive Information Redaction Framework), which retrieves domain-specific definitions based on the input's domain from a flexible knowledge base at inference time, needing no retraining to adapt. Two architectures, a three-call multi-agent pipeline and a single-agent variant, are evaluated across ten small open-weight models and eight datasets, including out-of-distribution fictional domains, against the OpenAI Privacy Filter (OPF) as a trained-classifier baseline. With only a few dozen expert-authored definitions per domain and no training data, ASIRF's recall exceeds OPF's in 68 of 80 model-domain combinations (85 percent), by at least one of the two architectures, with shortfalls confined mostly to OPF's training-distribution domains.

items.title: Towards An LLM-Driven Unified Conversion Framework for BT and FSM in Autonomous Intelligent Systems
items.summary: Finite state machine (FSM) and behavior trees (BT) are widely adopted behavioral modeling paradigms for autonomous intelligent systems. While functionally equivalent and inter-convertible in principle, existing transformation methods between FSM and BT face major challenges in preserving behavioral completeness and avoiding model complexity explosion. To overcome these issues, we propose an LLM-driven unified conversion framework that enables automatic, efficient, and semantically consistent transformation between FSM and BT. Specifically, a novel loop execution BT structure is designed for LLM to accurately capture the loop structure in FSM, thereby preserving behavioral completeness. To mitigate the state explosion problem in BT-to-FSM conversion, a depth compression strategy is introduced with LLM prompt to eliminate redundant control nodes, complemented by differentiated hierarchical conversion rules that collectively reduce the number of required sub-FSM. Simulation experiments in multiple autonomous decision-making scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework enables an accurate and automated bidirectional conversion between FSM and BT. Furthermore, it significantly enhances the scalability and maintainability of generated models compared to traditional approaches, providing a practical solution for behavior model conversion in consumer-grade autonomous intelligent systems such as service robots, game agents, and smart home devices

items.title: Policy as Code: A Coroutine-Bridge Harness for Fast-Reasoning Reliability on CAR-bench
items.summary: CAR-bench evaluates whether tool-using agents stay reliable under real-world uncertainty, executing every tool inside the evaluator so that each tool-result exchange is a separate agent round-trip. A conventional next-action agent can batch parallel tool calls, but a chain of dependent calls costs it one model call per round of results. We present a coroutine-bridge harness in which the model's only action is to emit a Python program that blocks and resumes in place across evaluator tool exchanges. This decouples model invocation from tool round-trips: on the public test split the agent uses a median of two model calls against seven agent turns per task, resolving a full multi-turn task in a median of 1.8 s of model latency on Cerebras gpt-oss-120b. Because the action surface is executable code, deterministic CAR-bench policies are encoded directly as logic in the tool layer rather than as prompt rules, enforcing compliance at zero reasoning cost. On the official hidden evaluation the harness won Track 2 with 60.0% Pass^3, 4.5x the organizer baseline, at the lowest estimated cost and the fastest median task latency (3.14 s) of any entry scoring above that baseline; the same unchanged harness reproduced an identical 60.0% Pass^3 on GPT-5.5 in the Open track, matching frontier-model agents. A single static prompt, appended with per-task state at the tail, stays byte-identical across calls and across tasks: the frozen submission prompt served 78% of input tokens from cache (86.6% across its warm tail), against 73% over a three-week development corpus in which prompt edits repeatedly reset the cache. This compounds the few-call design into a small fraction of nominal input compute.

items.title: Baszta: Data-Centric Fine-Tuning of a Polish Multi-Label Safety Classifier
items.summary: We develop a multi-label Polish content-safety classifier by fine-tuning allegro/herbert-base-cased (124M) across five categories (hate, vulgarity, sexual content, crime, self-harm) using a Focal + R-Drop objective, and evaluate the resulting model against Bielik Guard (S\'ojka) on the shared out-of-distribution Gadzi J\k{e}zyk benchmark. Both systems are given per-category threshold tuning on the same calibration split. Under that matched protocol our model holds a small but statistically significant lead in micro F1, while an apparent macro-F1 lead does not survive: it was an artifact of comparing a tuned model against an untuned one. We also report what that micro figure is worth. Because Gadzi J\k{e}zyk is 97% crime-positive, a classifier that flags crime on every input and nothing else already scores 0.910 micro F1 on the same test split, so micro separates neither system from a degenerate strategy and macro is the column that does. Per-category and per-protocol figures are reported in Section 4. The residual out-of-distribution gap is one of calibration rather than discrimination. Ranking quality stays high while positive probabilities collapse, and per-category temperature scaling recovers the loss where Platt scaling and isotonic regression do not. That recovery turns out to be conditional on the calibration set containing safe text. Gadzi J\k{e}zyk contains almost none, so thresholds fitted on it flag crime on every safe input, and a balanced refit buys a deployable operating point at the cost of adversarial recall. We report both operating points rather than only the flattering one. Two changes that are standard practice, per-class cost-sensitive weighting and mean pooling, each raise in-distribution macro F1 while lowering the out-of-distribution figure, which indicates that robustness has to be selected for directly rather than inherited from in-distribution accuracy.

items.title: From Text Decisions to Pixels: An Study of Jev-Style Visual Choice Model
items.summary: Visual software often needs a decision over supplied alternatives rather than a generated explanation. We present PixelJev, a native-image decision interface that maps an image, a task instruction, and a runtime candidate set to a structured choice and candidate-conditioned probabilities using small open multimodal models. Its initial realization unifies recognition and multiplechoice visual question answering through an existing language-model readout, with separately evaluated options for frozen inference, language-side adaptation, and held-out calibration. Across seven benchmark evaluations, 64-shot source adaptation raises Pets accuracy from 60.13% to 92.40% across optimization seeds and transfers to natural resampling, new texture labels, and A-OKVQA without target fitting, while frozen inference already supports both VQA tasks. A matched prompt-only follow-up on Pets and ScienceQA attributes the large Pets gain to adaptation and identifies a narrower output validity benefit of candidate readout in adapted VQA. Specialist DINOv2 probes remain stronger on source recognition, frozen 4B is stronger than adapted 2B on DTD and ScienceQA, and accuracy gains do not ensure calibrated target probabilities. These findings establish a working starting point for general-purpose visual decision models and identify the remaining requirements: schema robustness, cross-family transfer, and reliable use of visual evidence.

items.title: When No One Owns the Judgment: Accountability Under Contribution Dissolution in Human-AI Collaboration
items.summary: Communities often respond to potentially AI-assisted work by asking three questions: Was AI used? Was that use disclosed? Can hidden use be detected? These questions place AI use itself at the center of accountability while overlooking a deeper problem: unowned judgment. Evaluations, claims, decisions, and creative directions can be shaped by AI with no accountable human or institution prepared to stand behind them. We develop this argument through two illustrative cases: AI-assisted peer review and concealed AI use in creative work. The first shows how contribution dissolution can weaken responsibility while the second shows how the fear of losing credit can discourage honest disclosure. The cases expose the limits of disclosure rules and provenance records as responses to AI-mediated collaboration. We offer three directions for discussion: distinguishing the roles AI plays, identifying judgments that require clear human ownership, and creating conditions in which AI involvement can be disclosed without default penalty. The broader aim is to make AI-shaped contributions discussable, creditable, contestable, and repairable.

items.title: SkinAgent AI: A Safety-Grounded Multimodal Agentic Framework for Non-Diagnostic Skincare Support
items.summary: Consumer-facing skincare AI must coordinate visual evidence, product information, tool use, and user-facing actions within explicit evidence and safety boundaries. This study evaluates SkinAgent AI, a non-diagnostic multimodal framework that combines visual concern routing with grounded and auditable LLM-based orchestration. The architecture includes routing for Acne, Pores, and Wrinkles; photograph-based skin-type estimation; count-informed ordinal acne-severity support; typed tools; database-grounded recommendation and action functions; deterministic safety, privacy, and evidence checks; approval before state-changing actions; and structured trace and replay mechanisms. Visual-model performance and system-level agent behavior were evaluated separately. Across three seeds, the skin-condition routing model achieved 99.84% +/- 0.07% accuracy. Skin-type estimation achieved 88.85% accuracy, while count-informed acne-severity support achieved 84.59% accuracy with a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.9076. On a locked but non-independent 240-case system benchmark, intent accuracy was 80.00%, exact tool-set match was 62.92%, and strict task completion was 47.08%. No violations or successful cross-user leakage events were observed in the finite safety and privacy test suites. Tool-selection errors, incomplete grounding of product attributes, and unreliable failure fallback nevertheless remained. These findings support the feasibility of bounded, database-grounded, and traceable agent orchestration for non-diagnostic skincare assistance. They do not establish clinical readiness, external generalization, formal privacy guarantees, or universal safety. Independent validation, expert assessment, robustness and fairness testing, and prospective evaluation in real-world settings remain necessary.

items.title: The Last Human Gate: Forward Deployed Engineering for Governance Automation
items.summary: Enterprise governance requires decisions, evidence, and accountable authority; it does not require every review task to retain its current human implementation. We develop a task-substitution framework for Digital Governance Frameworks (DGF), treating each gate as an executable contract. Substitution requires sufficient accessible information, valid decision and authority checks, and a reduction in total human work after exceptions, verification, correction, and maintenance are counted. We derive a residual-work threshold and show why automating most cases can still increase labor. Forward deployed engineering connects these conditions to an architecture for agents, rule engines, evidence services, and escalation. DGF-Bench supplies controlled evidence from 300 synthetic projects and 899 evaluable model-project runs. Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-5.6 Luna, and DeepSeek v4.1 Flash achieve strict gate success of 94.98%, 83.29%, and 74.18%; complete-route success is 76.92%, 42.33%, and 24.67%. A deterministic control passes all 1,700 gates given the supplied rules and structured facts, locating the comparison in execution of a supplied decision kernel. Evidence audits and 135 repeated runs distinguish correct decisions from reliable execution. A document counterexample establishes an information-sufficiency obstruction. These results support the technical feasibility of replacing human execution of specified governance-review tasks with agents and software. The framework specifies a workforce test based on the complete human effort required at fixed output and quality; the present measurements concern review performance. Sources, dossiers, traces, and analyses are public.

items.title: Beyond Simple Input-Output Assessment Tasks: Leveraging Automated Programming Assessment for Non-Trivial Courses
items.summary: This paper discusses leveraging automated programming assessment for courses covering AI and machine learning foundations, highlighting its application in diverse fields.

items.title: An auditable conditional-strategy framework for open-ended decision-making in complex lung cancer
items.summary: This research presents an auditable conditional-strategy framework for open-ended decision-making in complex lung cancer, exemplified by the MedGPT Clinical Explorer.

items.title: Wearable ECG Quality Assessment: A Deep Learning and Ambulatory Context-Awareness Approach
items.summary: This paper introduces a Deep Learning-based signal quality assessment model for evaluating wearable ECG data, aiming to distinguish between clean and noisy ambulatory electrocardiograms.

items.title: Clinical Knowledge Graphs for Chest X-Ray Device Reasoning
items.summary: This paper presents uncertainty-aware clinical knowledge graphs designed to improve reasoning about medical device positioning in chest X-rays.

items.title: SMILESGNN: Interpretable Clinical Toxicity Prediction via SMILES-Graph Cross-Attention Fusion
items.summary: This research introduces SMILESGNN, a method for interpretable clinical toxicity prediction that uses SMILES-Graph cross-attention fusion to overcome challenges in drug discovery.

items.title: CFD Correction of Open Tip Clearance Flow in a Compressor Cascade Using VAE Latent Space Adaptation
items.summary: This study proposes a non-intrusive CFD correction method for open tip clearance flow in compressor cascades, utilizing variational autoencoder latent space adaptation.

items.title: SpaFactor: Lightweight Spatial Context-Aware Gene Program Modeling for Histology-to-Transcriptomics Inference
items.summary: This research introduces SpaFactor, a lightweight spatial context-aware gene program modeling method for inferring transcriptomics from histology images, offering a scalable alternative to spatial transcriptomics.

items.title: Leakage-Safe Machine Learning for Hydrogen Embrittlement Detection in 316L Stainless Steel: A Region-Held-Out Evaluation of Texture and Deep Features in SEM Micrographs
items.summary: This research proposes leakage-safe machine learning methods for detecting hydrogen embrittlement in 316L stainless steel using SEM micrographs, focusing on robust evaluation of texture and deep features.

items.title: TAM-Chain: Multi-Scale Thyroid Cytology Classification via Absorbing Markov Chains and Shannon Entropy Uncertainty Quantification for False-Negative Suppression and Domain-Shift Adaptation
items.summary: This research proposes TAM-Chain for multi-scale thyroid cytology classification using deep learning, aiming to suppress false-negative rates and adapt to domain shifts in thyroid cancer detection. It applies AI techniques to improve diagnostic accuracy in medical imaging.

items.title: Learning to Discover Interesting Mathematics
items.summary: This paper explores how Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly solving advanced mathematical problems, suggesting their potential to significantly expand mathematical knowledge. It focuses on the application of AI in mathematical discovery.

items.title: Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning for Joint Wire Calibration and Interaction Position Reconstruction in Multi-Wire Parallel Plate Avalanche Counters
items.summary: This research introduces physics-informed self-supervised learning to enhance joint wire calibration and interaction position reconstruction in multi-wire parallel plate avalanche counters. It aims to improve the accuracy and adaptability of scientific instrument calibration.

items.title: RLVR landscapes for iterated multiplications can be benign: Insights from spin-glass theory
items.summary: This research studies the optimization landscape of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) on algorithmic tasks, drawing insights from spin-glass theory. It investigates the capacity of RLVR to learn new reasoning capabilities.

items.title: OPDiv: Optimal Selection of Top-K High-Scoring, Diverse Compounds
items.summary: OPDiv presents a method for the optimal selection of a top-K set of high-scoring and diverse compounds from virtual screening campaigns. It addresses the tradeoff between compound ranking and diversity for practical applications.

items.title: Thinking Leakage: A Causal Audit of NoThink Post-Training in Hybrid Reasoning Models
items.summary: This research conducts a causal audit of "thinking leakage" in hybrid reasoning models post-trained in NoThink mode, where performance gains might stem from base model behavior. It aims to understand the underlying mechanisms of these models.

items.title: Upholding Robustness in Federated Learning: Trends, Emerging Strategies, and Research Opportunities
items.summary: This work synthesizes trends, emerging strategies, and research opportunities to uphold robustness in Federated Learning (FL). It addresses various challenges, including performance risks, information-stealing threats, and aggregation vulnerabilities.

items.title: Policy Complexity, Reaction Time, and Bounded Rationality in Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the impact of policy complexity, reaction time, and bounded rationality on reinforcement learning, drawing parallels with how cognitive constraints shape learning in biological agents. It explores fundamental aspects of AI learning mechanisms.

items.title: Evaluating Cross-region Generalization for Wavelet-Diffusion Precipitation Downscaling
items.summary: This study evaluates the cross-region generalization of wavelet-diffusion models (WDM) for kilometer-scale precipitation downscaling. It assesses their performance in geographically unseen areas and various event regimes.

items.title: The Mechanics of Delta Learning: Target Design for Generalizable Scientific Machine Learning
items.summary: This paper investigates the mechanics of $\Delta$-learning in scientific machine learning, where models are trained on residual errors relative to physical baselines. It analyzes the sufficiency of residual scale as a heuristic for performance improvement.

items.title: Monitoring Urban Traffic Dynamics at Fine Spatiotemporal Resolution Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Deep Learning
items.summary: This research demonstrates the use of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) combined with Deep Learning for monitoring urban traffic dynamics at fine spatiotemporal resolution. It offers a solution for real-time traffic monitoring in transportation research.

items.title: When Does Unsupervised Learning Succeed or Fail? A PoS Perspective on Reconstruction-Based Anomaly Detection
items.summary: This research analyzes when reconstruction-based unsupervised learning succeeds or fails in anomaly detection, characterizing failure modes through the Pursuit of Subspaces hypothesis. It provides a theoretical perspective on AI learning.

items.title: Image Fidelity is Not Field Fidelity: Joint Thermodynamic Reconstruction and Error Localization in Neural Tomography
items.summary: This research addresses the challenge of thermodynamic reconstruction and error localization in neural tomography, where neural fields optimize 3D physical fields from 2D images. It highlights that image fidelity does not guarantee field fidelity.

items.title: Response-state Learning for Transferable Vibrational Spectroscopic Characterization with Electron Prior
items.summary: This paper introduces Response-state Learning for transferable vibrational spectroscopic characterization, using an electron prior and SO(3) Equivariant Neural Kal. It aims to improve prediction accuracy across various chemical spaces.

items.title: Automatic Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation in Large Language Models via lp Regularization
items.summary: This paper introduces a new method using lp regularization for automatic rank allocation in Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for large language models, addressing a key challenge in parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

items.title: Growth-Inspired Graph Generation and Inverse Design of Mechanical Lattices via Dot Matrices Database Augmentation and GCNN
items.summary: This work presents a morphogenetic graph-generation framework, inspired by natural growth, for the inverse design of mechanical lattices, using Graph Convolutional Neural Networks and dot matrices database augmentation.

items.title: Generative Atmospheric Super-Resolution from Heterogeneous In Situ Observations through Composable Interfaces
items.summary: This paper investigates using generative AI, specifically diffusion models, to achieve super-resolution for atmospheric data from sparse and heterogeneous in-situ observations.

items.title: Physics and Data Driven Transformer-Mamba Framework for Flow Field
items.summary: This paper introduces the Transformer-Mamba for Flow Field (TM4FF) framework, a physics and data-driven deep learning method to accelerate and improve solving partial differential equations in computational fluid dynamics.

items.title: Downside-Controlled Online Forecast Combination under Delayed and Revised Outcomes
items.summary: This paper proposes a method for online forecast combination that provides downside control when adjusting predictions from a frozen foundation model, especially with delayed and revised outcomes.

items.title: A Particle-Swarm-Assisted Gradient Meta-Learning Algorithm for Joint Transmit Precoding and STAR-RIS Coefficient Optimization
items.summary: This paper proposes a particle-swarm-assisted gradient meta-learning algorithm to jointly optimize the transmit precoder and STAR-RIS coefficients for maximizing the weighted sum rate in multi-user downlink systems.

items.title: Edge AI on Constrained Devices for Binary Sleep-Wake Classification in Dynamic Environments
items.summary: This paper presents an Edge AI system designed for resource-constrained embedded hardware to perform binary sleep-wake classification in dynamic mobile environments, overcoming motion artifacts.

items.title: FB-GDM: Fully-Bayesian Guided Diffusion Models for High-Dimensional Linear Inverse Problems via Unsupervised Variational Inference
items.summary: This paper introduces FB-GDM (Fully-Bayesian Guided Diffusion Models), a new method for guiding diffusion models to solve high-dimensional linear inverse problems using unsupervised variational inference.

items.title: Online Task Adaptation via Self-Organisation
items.summary: This research investigates task-specific neural network adaptation that emerges from a meta-learned self-organizing process using Neural Cellular Automata, without relying on traditional gradient updates.

items.title: Beyond Feature Reliability: Repeat-Informed Multifractal Curve Regression for Brain-Age Prediction
items.summary: This paper introduces repeat-informed multifractal curve regression for brain-age prediction from resting-state fMRI, aiming to better characterize age-related changes in brain dynamics.

items.title: Neuralized Multi-Wavelet Decomposition for Time Series Classification and Forecasting
items.summary: This research proposes Neuralized Multi-Wavelet Decomposition, a new method for time series classification and forecasting that captures multiscale characteristics and complex frequency structures.

items.title: TinyCardioUNet: IMU-to-ECG Translation with Graph-Encoded Inter-Axis Dependencies and Tensor Decomposition-Based Parameter Reduction
items.summary: This paper introduces TinyCardioUNet, a lightweight UNet model that translates IMU data to ECG signals for continuous heart rate monitoring, featuring graph-encoded inter-axis dependencies and parameter reduction.

items.title: On the second-order optimization for spiking neural networks
items.summary: This paper investigates second-order optimization methods to address the challenging training of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), which typically suffer from a sharp loss landscape.

items.title: Lightweight Probabilistic Downscaling from a Deterministic Base Model
items.summary: This paper presents a lightweight probabilistic method for downscaling climate data, improving spatial resolution from global model outputs, building on advancements in machine learning for weather forecasting.

items.title: MORE-PLR: multi-output regression employed for partial label ranking
items.summary: This paper introduces MORE-PLR (multi-output regression employed for partial label ranking), a supervised learning method designed to predict a preference order over a subset of labels for a given input instance.

items.title: ICE: Task-Aligned Clifford Latent Fields for Multimodal Graph Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper proposes Task-Aligned Clifford Latent Fields as a new representation method for building multimodal graph foundation models, aiming to preserve entity semantics and interaction states across diverse data.

items.title: Neural Transport Nested Sampling
items.summary: This paper develops Neural Transport Nested Sampling (NTNS), a novel algorithm that combines neural density estimation with nested sampling for efficient sampling from Boltzmann distributions in molecular systems.

items.title: An Explainable DistilBERT-BiLSTM-Attention Framework for Binary and Multi-Class Hate Speech Detection
items.summary: The paper introduces an explainable DistilBERT-BiLSTM-Attention framework for binary and multi-class hate speech detection, presenting a new methodology for an AI application.

items.title: PTC-Bias: Phoneme-Level Temporal Competition for Bias Retrieval and Post-Decoding Correction in Speech LLMs
items.summary: This research proposes PTC-Bias, a two-stage phoneme-level temporal competition framework for improving rare-word recognition in speech Large Language Models through efficient bias retrieval.

items.title: Temporal Taxation Compounds Under Post-Training Compression of Whisper Models
items.summary: This study investigates how post-training compression techniques like quantization and pruning affect the demographic fairness of Automatic Speech Recognition models, such as Whisper.

items.title: Technical Manual for Toolkit for Confidence-Corpus Consistency via Fine-Tuning on a Fabricated Corpus
items.summary: A technical manual documents an open toolkit designed to test language model confidence by fine-tuning a causal language model on a fabricated corpus, detailing a method for model analysis.

items.title: Script Choice in LLMs: Evidence for Late-Layer Commitment
items.summary: This paper investigates how script knowledge is distributed across LLM layers using interpretability methods, revealing insights into the internal workings of language models.

items.title: ELF-REG: Scaling Continuous Diffusion Language Models to Reasoning Tasks
items.summary: This work explores ELF-REG, a method for scaling continuous diffusion language models to challenging reasoning tasks, aiming to establish their performance comparable to autoregressive LLMs.

items.title: Tag-Aware Structured Text Translation: Towards a Systematic Understanding
items.summary: This paper discusses Tag-Aware Structured Text Translation using LLMs, addressing the challenge of balancing translation fluency with the fidelity of structural and semantic tags in internet texts.

items.title: EAGER: Enhancing Generative Event Extraction via Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: EAGER is presented as a reinforcement learning framework designed to enhance generative event extraction by Large Language Models, focusing on simultaneous identification and classification.

items.title: Post-Training Leaves Behavioral Shadows on Unrelated Decisions
items.summary: This research finds that language models can transfer capabilities through task-unrelated text after post-training, demonstrating how behavioral shadows can impact unrelated decisions.

items.title: Grammatical "grandmother neurons" are rare in LLMs
items.summary: This paper investigates the interpretability of Large Language Models, specifically questioning the rarity of grammatical 'grandmother neurons' and how LLMs encode linguistic structures.

items.title: Parts-of-Speech as Emergent Categories in SAE Latent Space
items.summary: This research investigates whether morpho-syntactic information, specifically parts-of-speech, emerges as categories in the latent space of language models when inspected using Sparse AutoEncoders.

items.title: Baseline Shape Decides the Verdict: A Controlled Re-Examination of Ternary Language Models at 60K Parameters
items.summary: This study re-examines ternary language models at 60K parameters, investigating how architectural baseline shapes influence their performance, particularly in the sub-1M-parameter regime for microcontroller applications.

items.title: Large Language Models for Programming: Actually Fixing or Reimplementing Incorrect Code?
items.summary: This research investigates whether Large Language Models for programming actually fix or merely reimplement incorrect code, exploring their capabilities in problem-solving and bug-fixing contexts.

items.title: agentic-ger: terminology recovery in long-form speech using global context
items.summary: This research introduces agentic-ger, a method using large language models and global context for improved terminology recovery in long-form speech, addressing challenges in transcribing domain-specific terms.

items.title: YODAS v3: Over 1 Million Hours of High-Bandwidth, Stereophonic, Multilingual Speech
items.summary: YODAS v3 is introduced as the largest open speech dataset to date, providing over 1.1 million hours of high-bandwidth, stereophonic, multilingual speech across 147 languages under a CC BY 3.0 license.

items.title: What a Cross-Model Fixed-Point Census Can and Cannot Arbitrate About Repetition
items.summary: This research investigates two competing accounts for neural text degeneration, specifically repetition in output, using a cross-model fixed-point census to arbitrate between training data and network-based causes.

items.title: ModularSQL: A Runtime Guardrail for the Multiplicity Blind Spot in Text-to-SQL
items.summary: ModularSQL is presented as a runtime guardrail for Text-to-SQL systems, designed to prevent multiplicity errors and improve reliability by addressing the "multiplicity blind spot" in database query generation.

items.title: TTLab at AlexandriaX-2026: A Fine-Tuned Surface Tagger for Arabic Machine-Translation Error-Span Detection and Classification
items.summary: This submission describes TTLab's fine-tuned surface tagger system for Arabic Machine Translation error span detection and classification, framing the task as token-level classification.

items.title: How To Do Things With Prompts
items.summary: This paper examines the pragmatic features of directive speech acts when users interact with large language models, highlighting differences from everyday conversation and traditional human-computer interaction.

items.title: Confident but Wrong: A Constrained Decoding Diagnostic for Low-Resource Automatic Post-Editing
items.summary: This work introduces a black-box, inference-time diagnostic for Automatic Post-Editing (APE) in low-resource languages, designed to identify why APE systems fail to improve Machine Translation.

items.title: Named Entity Recognition using Sliding Window Approach
items.summary: This paper presents an inference-only pipeline for Named Entity Recognition (NER) that uses a sliding window approach to address limitations of transformer-based models with long documents.

items.title: DP-IPI: A Hybrid Differential Privacy Text Rewriting Mechanism for Indirect Personal Identifiers in Clinical Texts
items.summary: This paper proposes DP-IPI, a hybrid Differential Privacy text rewriting mechanism designed to prevent re-identification by handling indirect personal identifiers in clinical texts.

items.title: TTLab at StanceEval-2026: A Cloze-Style Prompting Approach for Arabic-Language Stance Detection (CLASP-Ar)
items.summary: This submission describes TTLab's cloze-style prompting approach (CLASP-Ar) for Arabic-language stance detection, aiming to improve performance and transferability over traditional multitask learning and ensemble methods.

items.title: Small yet Assistive: Spatially-Aware Post-Training for Low Vision
items.summary: Focuses on improving vision-language models (VLMs) to provide more precise, spatially-aware descriptions for blind and low-vision users, enabling safer navigation.

items.title: DrGait: Biomechanically Grounded Visual Reasoning for Interpretable Clinical Gait Analysis
items.summary: Introduces DrGait, a method using biomechanically grounded visual reasoning to provide interpretable clinical gait analysis, addressing VLM limitations in medical applications.

items.title: M$^2$PFN: End-to-End Disentangled Alignment for Generalizable Multimodal In-Context Learning in Alzheimer's Disease
items.summary: Introduces M$^2$PFN, a method for generalizable multimodal in-context learning, designed to improve the diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease by combining imaging and tabular data.

items.title: Looks the Same, Answers Differently: Flip-Direction Steering for Robust Vision-Language Reasoning
items.summary: Explores how subtle image changes affect Vision-Language Models' reasoning and proposes "Flip-Direction Steering" to improve robustness in VLM reasoning.

items.title: Multimodal Routing and Region Refinement for Language-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: Proposes a method using multimodal routing and region refinement to improve language-guided medical image segmentation, aiming to reduce ambiguity in delineating findings.

items.title: Direction-Scale Decomposition in Action Representation: Rethinking What to Tokenize for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Investigates action representation in discrete-token Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, proposing "Direction-Scale Decomposition" to improve action tokenization and overcome limitations of conventional representations.

items.title: Exploiting Target Knowledge from MLLMs for Robust Few-Shot Segmentation
items.summary: Proposes a method to improve robust few-shot segmentation by exploiting target knowledge extracted from Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for efficient adaptation to novel object categories.

items.title: Passive LWIR Hyperspectral Ranging via Transmittance Extraction and Distance Alignment
items.summary: Describes a method for passive long-wave infrared (LWIR) hyperspectral ranging, which estimates distance in low-light conditions by exploiting atmospheric absorption features in thermal radiance.

items.title: EIB-Net: Entropy-Guided Information Bottleneck for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection
items.summary: This paper introduces EIB-Net, a method using an entropy-guided information bottleneck to improve the detection of AI-generated images and generalize across various generative models. It addresses the challenge of identifying synthetic images that lack typical manipulation artifacts.

items.title: WildHSR: Metric Feed-Forward 4D People-Scene Reconstruction from a 3D Foundation Model
items.summary: This research introduces WildHSR, a method for metric feed-forward 4D people-scene reconstruction using a 3D foundation model. It aims to solve the missing metric scale and persistent person identity required for joint reconstruction from existing up-to-scale representations.

items.title: Spectral Amplitude Purification in Distribution Matching for Diffusion Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces Spectral Amplitude Purification, a technique designed to improve Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) for diffusion models. The method addresses issues with low-frequency signal dominance in DMD to enhance the recovery of fine-grained details in diffusion sampling.

items.title: UpDown-SC: Gravity-Canonicalized Dual-Envelope Scan Context for Indoor LiDAR Place Recognition
items.summary: This research proposes UpDown-SC, a gravity-canonicalized dual-envelope scan context method to improve indoor LiDAR place recognition. It enhances retrieval robustness by addressing changes in sensor attitude or mounting height between mapping and query sessions.

items.title: Less is More: Encoder-only Audio-Visual Segmentation
items.summary: This research proposes an encoder-only architecture for Audio-Visual Semantic Segmentation, aiming to identify, segment, and classify sound-emitting objects in video frames. It suggests that previous Transformer-based methods, inherited from image segmentation, contain redundancies.

items.title: FoCal: Frequency-Oriented Cross-Modal Interaction and Spectral Calibration for Aerial Visible-Infrared Object Detection
items.summary: This research introduces FoCal, a method for aerial visible-infrared object detection that uses frequency-oriented cross-modal interaction and spectral calibration. It aims to improve robust perception by exploiting complementary information across modalities under complex conditions.

items.title: Recoverable Geographic Location Information in Earth-Observation Embeddings
items.summary: This research investigates the extent to which geographic location information is recoverable from embeddings generated by Earth-observation foundation models. It explores the implications for location-aware applications and potential detriments when geographic invariance is desired.

items.title: An Automated Georeferencing Technique for Multi-Temporal Stope Point Clouds for Downstream Geotechnical Analysis
items.summary: This paper presents an automated georeferencing technique for multi-temporal stope point clouds acquired from UAV laser scanning in underground mines. The method supports downstream geotechnical analysis in GNSS-denied environments.

items.title: ImCorr: Sub-pixel Semantic Correspondence via Implicit Feature Decoding
items.summary: This research introduces ImCorr, a method designed to achieve sub-pixel semantic correspondence by using implicit feature decoding. It addresses the limitation of current methods that plateau at fine-grained thresholds due to grid-tied readouts.

items.title: FounRef: Robust, Structure-Preserving, and Fast Metric Refinement of Frozen Monocular Foundation Priors with Sparse Anchors
items.summary: This research proposes FounRef, a method for robust, structure-preserving, and fast metric refinement of frozen monocular foundation priors using sparse anchors. It addresses the challenge of achieving accurate, faithful, and fast dense metric depth from cameras for 3D applications.

items.title: SARFusion: Scene-Aware Routing Fusion for Robust Camera-LiDAR 3D Object Detection
items.summary: This research proposes SARFusion, a scene-aware routing fusion method for robust camera-LiDAR 3D object detection in autonomous driving. It aims to improve performance under corrupted driving conditions by addressing strong inter-modality dependencies in existing fusion detectors.

items.title: Deep learning of longitudinal visual fields predicts glaucoma progression rate and identifies fast progressors
items.summary: This research demonstrates how deep learning can predict the progression rate of glaucoma from longitudinal visual fields, enabling the identification of fast progressors. This approach aims to improve timely intervention and prevent irreversible blindness.

items.title: Hyperbolic Multimodal Continual Learning: A Closest-Admissible Solution
items.summary: This research proposes a closest-admissible solution for Hyperbolic Multimodal Continual Learning, which explicitly preserves the Lorentz geometry in hyperbolic multimodal models. This addresses limitations of existing continual-learning methods that don't maintain within-modality similarity and cross-modal correspondence.

items.title: A Study of the Limits of Collaborative DCT-Based Image Denoising via Interpretable Neural Networks
items.summary: This research explores the limits of collaborative DCT-based image denoising through the use of interpretable neural networks. It aims to provide insights into how modern deep neural networks achieve strong performance in image restoration.

items.title: Learning a Flow to Self-Supervised Representations
items.summary: This paper introduces Flow-Based Distribution Matching (FBDM), a non-adversarial framework for learning self-supervised representations using explicit geometric references, addressing costly encoder-critic optimization issues.

items.title: Domain Recentering and Confidence-Weighted Prior Calibration for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This research proposes domain recentering and confidence-weighted prior calibration to improve the performance of vision-language models like CLIP under distribution shift, without requiring per-sample optimization.

items.title: Shadow Reduction in Ultrasound Imaging Using Differentiable Simulation and Radiance Field Decomposition
items.summary: This paper presents a method using differentiable simulation and radiance field decomposition to reduce acoustic shadows in ultrasound imaging, particularly for improving fetal brain imaging.

items.title: A Hybrid CNN--State-Space--Attention Backbone with Joint-Embedding Predictive Pretraining for 12-Lead ECG Classification

items.title: When Misalignment Becomes Supervision: Structured Label Noise in Supervised Synthetic CT Generation
items.summary: This research investigates how residual misalignments in registered medical images can be used as structured label noise for supervised synthetic CT generation, improving training and evaluation.

items.title: DEdit: Iterative Draft Editing for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: DEdit introduces an iterative draft editing method for speculative decoding that uses diffusion-based drafters to propose multiple tokens simultaneously, aiming to reduce latency in autoregressive LLM generation. items.title: Strong Multilingual Privacy Tagging at Encoder Speed
items.summary: This paper describes the development of a strong multilingual named-entity tagger designed for privacy redaction, capable of fine-grained distinctions and supporting varied redaction policies while preserving textual relationships. It aims for efficient performance at encoder speed.

items.title: MetaSteer: Context-Conditioned, nonlinear Steering via Attention-Projection Adaptation
items.summary: MetaSteer proposes a novel method for context-conditioned, nonlinear steering of large language models through attention-projection adaptation, aiming to overcome limitations of linear, context-independent interventions in activation space. It addresses the information bottleneck of fixed representations.

items.title: Training LLM Judges from Language Feedback via Position-Selective Self-Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for training LLM judges from natural language feedback using position-selective self-distillation, particularly for subjective tasks where evaluation criteria weighting is crucial. It aims to improve upon outcome-supervised reinforcement learning approaches.

items.title: Recovering Off-Policy Supervision for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This research focuses on recovering lost off-policy supervision for speculative decoding's block drafters, aiming to resolve severe supervision loss that occurs when an off-policy token invalidates subsequent slots during training.

items.title: Scaling Parameter and Context in Attention: Native Sparse Attention from Mixture-of-Head
items.summary: This paper introduces "Native Sparse Attention from Mixture-of-Head" as a method to scale attention parameters and context length in language models, aiming to improve model quality and support longer contexts more efficiently.

items.title: Audible World Models: Spatially Aware Sound Generation for 3D Worlds

items.title: LongTake: Learning to Sustain Dynamics in Long-Horizon Video Generation
items.summary: This research introduces LongTake, a method that enables autoregressive video diffusion models to sustain dynamics and coherent scene evolution for long-horizon video generation.

items.title: StereoGaussians: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting from Stereo Images
items.summary: This paper introduces StereoGaussians, a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting method for 3D reconstruction from stereo images, addressing challenges in nearby-view extrapolation and rendering newly exposed regions.

items.title: PixelUMM: Encoder-Free Unified Image and Video Understanding and Generation
items.summary: PixelUMM proposes an encoder-free unified multimodal model for image and video understanding and generation, simplifying integration with vision-language pretraining by operating directly in pixel space.

items.title: Exo2EgoHOI: Hand-Object-Interaction Aware Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
items.summary: Exo2EgoHOI presents a new method for generating egocentric videos from third-person manipulation videos, providing scalable visual experience data for embodied intelligence.

items.title: STEPS: Scene Text Editing with Preserved Style Using Diffusion and Contrastive Style Encoding
items.summary: STEPS introduces a novel diffusion model architecture for quality scene text editing, enabling text replacement in images while preserving the original style through contrastive style encoding.

items.title: ReGain: Restoring Subject Fidelity in Personalization on Synthetic Images
items.summary: ReGain is a method designed to restore subject fidelity in personalized text-to-image diffusion models, addressing the degradation that occurs when fine-tuning on synthetic images instead of real photographs.

items.title: EPIC: Epipolar-Consistent 360{\deg} Immersive Stereo Video Generation

items.summary: This paper proposes state-grounded transitions for streaming video generators, enabling more robust mid-stream prompt switching and dynamic modulation of video synthesis without cutting corners or taking heuristic shortcuts.

items.summary: This paper introduces KAME, a tandem speech-to-speech model architecture that uses a large language model (LLM) as an asynchronous text backend to guide natural conversational responses.

items.summary: This comprehensive study introduces HermNet, a new spectral graph neural network model constructed with Hermite polynomials, combining a nodewise predictor with normalized Hermite propagation. It offers a simplified architecture for graph-based AI tasks.

These models leverage structured reports and abnormality-focused text to capture both common and infrequent findings.

items.title: ComplexSync: High-Fidelity and Real-Time Lip Sync in Complex Scenarios
items.summary: This paper introduces ComplexSync, a method designed to achieve high-fidelity and real-time lip synchronization in complex scenarios. It addresses the limitations of diffusion models regarding inference latency and performance in challenging conditions.

items.title: TOLA: Text-aware One-Step Latent Adaptation for Diffusion-based Text Image Super-Resolution
items.summary: This paper introduces TOLA, a text-aware one-step latent adaptation method for diffusion-based text image super-resolution. It aims to improve text image readability under degradation while reducing the computational cost and inference latency of existing multi-step prediction methods.

items.title: IronViT: Toward Efficient Generalist Visual Representation Learning
items.summary: This paper presents IronViT, a new approach aimed at efficient generalist visual representation learning. It addresses the computational expense of softmax attention in current visual backbones at high resolutions, seeking a unified representation for various visual cues.
