items.title: Automated Evaluation of Multi-Turn Dialogues in In-Car Conversational Assistants
items.summary: Focuses on the automated evaluation of multi-turn dialogues in in-car conversational assistants. The research addresses challenges in ensuring reliability for these AI systems due to complex interactions and safety constraints.

items.title: How to Run Statistics over LLM Judges and Trust the Results: Calibrated Inference for Small-Sample AI Evaluation with evalstats
items.summary: Presents "evalstats," a framework for calibrated inference when evaluating AI using LLM judges and small samples. The work aims to provide reliable statistical methods for computing confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, and judge-bias corrections in AI evaluation.

items.title: $\tau$-Multilingual: Benchmarking Voice Agents Across Languages
items.summary: Introduces $\tau$-Multilingual, an extension of the $\tau$-Voice benchmark designed for evaluating voice agents across multiple languages. It includes native-speaker review and evaluation of generated language and spoken output in Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Hindi, Korean, and Mandarin.

items.title: CruxBench: A Benchmark of Information Discovery
items.summary: CruxBench is introduced as a new benchmark for large language models, designed to evaluate their ability to identify and decompose complex problems into relevant subquestions for information discovery.

items.title: CineSubBench: Evaluating LLMs on Long-Form Narrative and Cultural Understanding from Multilingual Movie Subtitles
items.summary: CineSubBench is introduced as a new benchmark to evaluate large language models on long-form narrative comprehension and cultural understanding using multilingual movie subtitles.

items.title: CoVLM-Bench: A Real-World Benchmark for Cooperative Driving Question Answering and Planning
items.summary: CoVLM-Bench is presented as a new real-world benchmark for evaluating Vision-Language Models in cooperative driving scenarios, specifically for question answering and planning.

items.title: AerialDojo-200K: A Large-Scale Benchmark Suite for Open-World Aerial Object-Goal Search
items.summary: AerialDojo-200K is introduced as a large-scale benchmark suite designed for evaluating open-world aerial object-goal search capabilities of aerial agents in unstructured three-dimensional environments.

items.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Synapse Detection and Proofreading in Connectomics
items.summary: This work benchmarks 21 vision-language models on synapse detection and proofreading tasks using electron microscopy images in connectomics, evaluating their performance in a medical application.

items.title: Foresight at the Event Boundary: Evaluating Physical Prediction in Video World Models
items.summary: This paper evaluates the physical prediction capabilities of video world models, analyzing current evaluation methods and their focus on reference similarity and physical-law consistency.

items.title: Beyond Legibility: Benchmarking Visual Text Rendering and In-Place Editing in Unified Video Generation
items.summary: This work introduces a benchmark for evaluating visual text rendering and in-place editing capabilities in unified video generation, focusing on text legibility and temporal stability.

items.title: Scaling Video Generation for Reasoning: At What Cost?
items.summary: This study investigates the reasoning capabilities and computational cost of scaled video generation models using a controlled benchmark involving predicting Rubik's Cube moves.

items.title: VLM4Cluster: Benchmarking Deep Clustering In the Era of Vision-Language Pre-training
items.summary: This work presents VLM4Cluster, a benchmark for evaluating deep clustering methods in the context of vision-language pre-training and language-assisted image clustering.

items.title: LIBERO-MAX: Do Robot Policies Adapt When the World Changes?
items.summary: This item introduces LIBERO-MAX, which investigates how robot policies adapt to changes in the environment, highlighting limitations of current simulation robustness benchmarks in evaluating temporal challenges.

items.title: RoboChrono: A Real Robot Benchmark for Streaming Task Understanding
items.summary: This item introduces RoboChrono, a new real robot benchmark comprising 39 scenarios and 34,713 evaluation instances, designed to assess models' ability to understand ongoing robot manipulation tasks based on visual observations and interaction history.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches the no-CoT performance of GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Sol demonstrated significantly improved performance on a task suite, nearly matching the capabilities of GPT-6 Astra in a direct model comparison.

items.title: LabBench: Can AI agents decide what experiment to run next?
items.summary: A new benchmark called LabBench is introduced to evaluate the ability of AI agents to autonomously decide on the next steps in scientific experiments. The platform assesses how well AI agents can make decisions in a wet-lab environment.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol comes close to Astra at a fifth of the price
items.summary: OpenAI's internal benchmarks indicate that the new GPT-6.1 Sol model performs almost as well as GPT-6 Astra, but at one-fifth of the cost, while Astra is delayed due to safety concerns.

items.title: Human or AI?: A Baroque Music Quiz
items.summary: A blind listening quiz was created to test if listeners can distinguish between Baroque music composed by humans and music generated by LLMs like GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.

items.title: Anthropic's mid-tier Claude climbs the rankings - The Rundown AI
items.summary: Anthropic's mid-tier Claude AI model has improved its performance in various rankings, indicating stronger capabilities compared to competitors.

items.title: Auditing System-1 Models on Biosecurity-Relevant Benchmarks: Calibration, Selective Prediction, and Permutation Instability in a Non-Generative Model
items.summary: This study audits non-generative 'System-1' models on biosecurity-relevant benchmarks, evaluating their calibration, selective prediction, and permutation instability to assess reliability.

items.title: In-Context Binding Capacity in Language Models
items.summary: This research measures the in-context binding capacity of language models by quantifying how many entity-value assignments they can recall before losing track. It uses continuous recall curves and threshold sweeps to compare this limit across various open models.

items.title: When 10,000 Windows Are Not 10,000 Tests: Auditing Statistical Confidence in Sliding-Window Time-Series Classification
items.summary: This paper critiques the evaluation of sliding-window time-series classifiers, arguing that thousands of overlapping test windows do not represent independent tests. It calls for auditing statistical confidence in current evaluation methods due to shared observations and nested predictions.

items.title: Check twice, cut once with LLM search relevance eval
items.summary: The article discusses evaluation methods for large language models, specifically focusing on assessing their search relevance.

items.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Overtakes GPT-6 in A.I. Ranking - trendingtopics.eu
items.summary: Claude Sonnet 5.5 has reportedly surpassed GPT-6 in a recent AI ranking, indicating its competitive performance in the AI model landscape.

items.title: EnigmaForge – an LLM benchmark where the question is hidden in the story
items.summary: EnigmaForge is introduced as a new benchmark for large language models, designed to evaluate their ability to find hidden questions within a story.

items.title: Gemini 3.5 Transcribe vs OpenAI’s GPT-Transcribe
items.summary: This article provides a side-by-side comparison of Google's Gemini 3.5 Transcribe and OpenAI's GPT-Transcribe models, detailing their development, use cases, and performance metrics.

items.title: Artificial Analysis launches Cyber Index for AI-powered cyber defense - news.lavx.hu
items.summary: Artificial Analysis launches its new Cyber Index, designed to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of AI-powered cyber defense systems.

items.title: MiniMax M3.1 vs GPT-6 Luna vs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: 3x Price Gap [2026] - tech-insider.org
items.summary: The article compares several AI models, including MiniMax M3.1, GPT-6 Luna, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, highlighting their price differences.

items.title: Shark Tank judge Anupam Mittal says Elon Musk’s Grok is faster and cheaper than Anthropic’s Claude: 'I fe - The Times of India
items.summary: A judge from Shark Tank compares Elon Musk's Grok and Anthropic's Claude, claiming Grok is faster and cheaper, thereby evaluating and comparing two specific AI models.

items.title: ScopeBench: Do Agents Preserve Engagement Boundaries Under Goal Pressure?
items.summary: ScopeBench is introduced as a new benchmark to evaluate whether AI agents can maintain engagement boundaries under goal pressure, particularly in web application and network penetration testing.

items.title: A Synthetic Ground-Truth Framework for the Evaluation of Explainable AI Methods
items.summary: A new synthetic ground-truth framework is proposed for evaluating Explainable AI (XAI) methods, addressing the challenge of lacking reliable evaluation procedures and ground truth explanations.

items.title: Do LLMs Understand Context? A Knowledge Graph-Based Evaluation Framework
items.summary: A knowledge graph-based evaluation framework is proposed to assess whether large language models (LLMs) truly understand context or merely excel at pattern matching.

items.title: BioEVAL: A global, multi-institutional benchmark of large language and multimodal models for bioengineering
items.summary: BioEVAL is introduced as a new global, multi-institutional benchmark designed to evaluate large language and multimodal models specifically for bioengineering tasks.

items.title: Benchy: towards a universal language for task-oriented AI benchmarks
items.summary: Benchy is presented as a semantic language and execution engine aimed at providing a universal framework for defining and running task-oriented AI benchmarks.

items.title: HARDEN: Constrained Evolutionary Search for Harder, Answer-Preserving Evaluation Cases
items.summary: Introduces HARDEN, a constrained evolutionary search method to create more challenging evaluation cases for language models while preserving their expected outputs. It aims to address the underrepresentation of complexity in current benchmarks for enterprise deployments.

items.title: ORCA: Evaluating LLMs on Data Science Code Translation
items.summary: Introduces ORCA, a method for evaluating large language models on Data Science Code Translation (DSCT), which involves converting code between different data science libraries. It assesses the models' ability to preserve functional equivalence and enable interoperability.

items.title: Backbone-Adaptive Evidence Routing for Robust Pairwise LLM Judging
items.summary: Introduces Backbone-Adaptive Evidence Routing (BAER), a method to adapt the evidence mechanism for robust pairwise LLM judges. It addresses the issue that no single evidence gathering protocol is optimal across all benchmarks and judge backbones.

items.title: Evaluating Real-Time Voice Agents: From Component Quality to Grounded Outcomes
items.summary: This paper discusses methods for evaluating real-time voice agents, moving beyond component quality to grounded outcomes. It highlights the fragmented literature across speech foundation modeling, turn-taking psycholinguistics, and agentic evaluation.

items.title: Same Text, Different Numbers: The Divergence of LLM-Based Measures
items.summary: This research investigates the divergence and invariance of LLM-based textual measures, such as sentiment and uncertainty, when applied to corporate text using different large language models.

items.title: A Benchmark Framework for Screening Automation in Systematic Reviews
items.summary: This research proposes a new benchmark framework for automating the screening phase in systematic reviews, aiming to evaluate and reduce the workload of article relevance classification using LLMs.

items.title: CARGO: Context-Aware Retrieval-Gated Evaluation of Agentic AI in Production
items.summary: CARGO is presented as a Context-Aware Retrieval-Gated Evaluation framework for assessing agentic AI systems in production environments, particularly when reference answers are not directly applicable.

items.title: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
items.summary: This paper addresses the need for better benchmarking of web agents, focusing on their ability to synthesize, organize, and display knowledge rather than just search, across complex multi-step workflows.

items.title: TRACE: Temporal Audit and Condition-aware Evaluation of Streaming Video Understanding
items.summary: TRACE is a new evaluation framework introduced for streaming video understanding, providing temporal audits and condition-aware metrics to assess models' ability to interpret evidence as it arrives.

items.title: Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4
items.summary: This paper evaluates Google's Gemma 4-e4b model's behavior when processing conflicting information, specifically how it prioritizes sources based on framing or presentation order.

items.title: Enhancing Assessment of Self-Consistency in LLM Explanations using Perturbation Strength
items.summary: This work proposes an LLM-as-a-judge approach to measure perturbation strength, aiming to enhance the assessment of self-consistency in LLM-generated explanations.

items.title: From annotation to reasoning: Culture in language models
items.summary: This paper explores how to evaluate language models for cultural understanding, questioning traditional benchmarks that focus on factual knowledge or predefined meanings.

items.title: Evaluating Sycophancy in Chinese Large Language Models on Factual Questions Derived from Online Search Queries
items.summary: This study evaluates sycophancy in Chinese large language models, assessing their tendency to align responses with user beliefs on factual questions derived from online search queries.

items.title: TrafficImag: A Benchmark for Counterfactual Roadside Traffic Video Generation
items.summary: TrafficImag is introduced as a new benchmark for counterfactual roadside traffic video generation, evaluating how well models can modify a selected actor in a scene while maintaining consistency with road topology and other traffic.

items.title: UltraG-Bench: A Multi-task Benchmark for assessing Large Vision-Language Models on Pixel-level Evidence Grounding in Ultrasound
items.summary: UltraG-Bench is introduced as a multi-task benchmark designed to assess Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on their ability to perform pixel-level evidence grounding in ultrasound images. It addresses the current lack of pixel-level visual evidence in VLM semantic predictions.

items.title: MVVBench: Benchmarking 4D Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: MVVBench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the 4D reasoning capabilities of vision-language models in multi-view video understanding.

items.title: CCRV-Bench: Constraint-Based Evaluation of Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: CCRV-Bench is a new benchmark for the constraint-based evaluation of causal reasoning capabilities in vision-language models, addressing the lack of reliable assessment in this area.

items.title: STORM-Bench: Evaluating Online Video QA under Evolving and Incomplete Evidence
items.summary: STORM-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate online video question answering systems under conditions of evolving and incomplete evidence, focusing on tracking state transitions.

items.title: Evaluation Is All You Need for Multi-Modal Autonomous Driving
items.summary: This paper highlights the critical role of evaluation in multi-modal planning for autonomous driving, aiming to improve trajectory representations and candidate distribution.

items.title: A Simple Puzzle Reveals the Jagged Edge of AI's Abilities
items.summary: A simple puzzle is used to highlight the uneven and inconsistent capabilities of artificial intelligence systems, revealing the "jagged edge" of their intelligence.

items.title: Claude vs Perplexity: Which AI Tool Should You Use in 2026? - Memeburn
items.summary: An article provides a comparison between Claude and Perplexity AI tools to guide users on which one to choose by 2026.

items.title: Musk Acknowledges Anthropic’s Fable 5 Beats xAI’s Grok 4.5 - tokenpost.com
items.summary: Elon Musk acknowledges that Anthropic's Fable 5 AI model outperforms xAI's Grok 4.5.

items.title: Qwen 27B vs Swift: 50% Faster Speeds Come at an Accuracy Cost - Geeky Gadgets
items.summary: A comparison is made between the Qwen 27B and Swift models, highlighting that 50% faster speeds come at an accuracy cost.

items.title: Show HN: Note Duel – LLM Arena for composing music
items.summary: A new platform called Note Duel, an 'LLM Arena,' is introduced for comparing and evaluating AI models in musical composition.

items.title: Alignment Forecasting: Predicting Misalignment from Training Data
items.summary: A new benchmark, AlignmentForecastBench, is introduced to study and predict AI model misalignment from training data before fine-tuning.

items.title: Spurious probes as a black-box alternative to activation probing
items.summary: Researchers describe 'spurious probes,' a black-box method using unrelated questions to reveal internal states of models and evaluate their behavior after capability benchmarks.

items.title: J-lens shouldn't target the final layer by default
items.summary: The article argues against targeting the final layer with J-lenses, citing issues like shifted language readouts and inflated evaluations when applied to models like DeepSeek-V3. It references Anthropic's work on J-lenses.

items.title: TW3Cast: A Frozen Router of Lightly Fine-Tuned Foundation Models for Time-Series Forecasting on GIFT-Eval, Selected Entirely on the Training Split
items.summary: TW3Cast, a time-series forecasting system, achieved position 3 on the GIFT-Eval benchmark, demonstrating its performance against other models in quantitative evaluation.

items.title: TWIST: A Proposed Benchmark for Intervention Quality in Conversational Memory, with a Human-Validated Draft-Alignment
items.summary: Introduces TWIST, a proposed benchmark suite designed to evaluate the intervention quality of deployed conversational memory systems, complementing existing recall benchmarks.

items.title: RECLAIM: Can Agents Reproduce the Claims of Machine Learning Papers?
items.summary: Introduces RECLAIM, a new benchmark comprising 100 NeurIPS papers, designed to assess the capability of AI agents to reproduce research claims and experimental results in machine learning.

items.title: PFArena: Benchmarking Language Models for Protein Modification
items.summary: Introduces PFArena, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of language models, including PLMs and LLM-based agents, in tasks related to protein modification.

items.title: SWE-Prometheus: Measuring Engineering Governance Improvements in Real-World Repositories
items.summary: This paper introduces SWE-Prometheus, a new benchmark designed to measure improvements in engineering governance for large language model-based coding agents in real-world software repositories.

items.title: Delay-of-Gratification as a Multi-Agent Survival Micro-benchmark for Long-Horizon LLMs: Social Exposure, Personas, and Tool Use Budgets
items.summary: This paper proposes a "Delay-of-Gratification" multi-agent survival micro-benchmark to quantify the long-horizon behavior of LLM agents, considering social exposure, personas, and tool use budgets.

items.title: UO-FIE: Combining Exact-Label Supervision with Graded Utility for Factivity Inference
items.summary: This paper introduces UO-FIE, an evaluation method for Factivity Inference Evaluation 2026 (FIE2026), which classifies Chinese context-hypothesis pairs into nine factivity intervals. The evaluation metric rewards both exact predictions and proximity to the correct interval.

items.title: Language Specificity vs. Domain Diversity: Benchmarking Transformers for Bangla Medical NER
items.summary: This work presents a comprehensive empirical benchmark evaluating fine-tuned transformer encoders for Medical Named Entity Recognition (NER) in Bangla, a low-resource language.

items.title: Benchmarking Argumentative Behaviour of LLMs: A Study of Defences Against Character Attacks
items.summary: This study focuses on benchmarking the argumentative behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), specifically evaluating their defenses against character attacks in persuasive dialogues.

items.title: COILD: An Indic-Centric Parallel Corpus and Benchmark for Machine Translation Across Indian Languages
items.summary: This item introduces COILD, a new Indic-centric parallel corpus and benchmark specifically designed for evaluating and improving machine translation across Indian languages.

items.title: Polite but Misaligned: Evaluating LLM Politeness Judgments Against Human Pragmatic Norms
items.summary: The research evaluates LLM politeness judgments against human pragmatic norms using English-language datasets, assessing how well models align with human social understanding.

items.title: Reasoning Instructions Can Break Answer Decoding in Vision--Language Models
items.summary: The paper reveals that certain reasoning instructions can distort multiple-choice Vision-Language Model evaluations when using CoT-prefix scoring, causing significant performance drops in models like Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

items.title: Where LLM Graders Succeed and Break: Evidence from Two Computer-Science Exams
items.summary: This research evaluates the performance of LLMs as graders for computer science exams, analyzing their success and pitfalls across various configurations and models. It provides evidence from grading a practical Computer Vision exam.

items.title: ArGuard Shared Task: Harmful Content Detection in Arabic Memes and LLM Prompts
items.summary: ArGuard is a shared task focused on harmful content detection in Arabic memes and LLM prompts, involving two tracks for multimodal hate detection and LLM safety evaluation, with 58 registered teams.

items.title: From Policy Documents to Structured Survey Responses: Evaluating Large Language Models for Policy Monitoring
items.summary: This paper evaluates the capability of large language models to transform information from policy documents into structured survey responses for efficient policy monitoring. It aims to reduce reliance on costly manual survey efforts.

items.title: BanglaTurn: A Benchmark and Whisper-Based Model for End-of-Turn Detection in Bangla Speech
items.summary: BanglaTurn is a new corpus and a Whisper-based model designed for end-of-turn detection in Bangla conversational speech, created by combining speaker diarization and LLM processing with human verification.

items.title: Likelihood Ranking doesn't Scale Like Prompting in LLMs
items.summary: This research examines LLM evaluation methods, comparing how likelihood ranking scales differently from prompting when assessing model performance, particularly in multiple-choice question answering.

items.title: Two Emojis of Difference: What Multilingual Affective Generation Benchmarks Actually Measure
items.summary: This audit investigates a multilingual affective generation benchmark, questioning what it truly measures by evaluating instruction-tuned LLMs producing emoji summaries across multiple languages and human judgments.

items.title: Evaluating Explanation-Driven Vision-Language Reasoning via Generation Order Interventions
items.summary: This research evaluates explanation-driven vision-language reasoning by using generation order interventions to assess how models produce and rely on explanations, particularly in relation to post-hoc paradigms.

items.title: PROOF: Profiling Reliability of Object-Level Facts in Large Language Models
items.summary: PROOF is a new profile-oriented benchmark designed to assess the reliability of object-level facts in instruction-tuned large language models, aiming to uncover detailed factuality issues beyond aggregate scores.

items.title: EnSiTa - A Trilingual Multi-Domain Parallel Dataset and Benchmark for Domain-Specific Machine Translation
items.summary: EnSiTa is a new trilingual multi-domain parallel dataset and benchmark for evaluating domain-specific machine translation, particularly for low-resource languages like Sinhala and Tamil against English.

items.title: Benchmarking Arabic--Russian Machine Translation: A Comparison of Fine-tuned NMT and Few-shot LLMs under Rich Morphology and Low Lexical Overlap
items.summary: This study benchmarks Arabic-Russian machine translation by comparing fine-tuned Neural Machine Translation models and few-shot Large Language Models, focusing on the challenges of rich morphology and low lexical overlap.

items.title: JEV vs. LLMs as Rubric Judges: Cheaper, Faster, and Wrong in the Same Places
items.summary: This research compares Jev, a typed classifier, with three flash-tier LLM judges on nine benchmark panels to assess their accuracy as rubric judges, finding Jev to be cheaper, faster, and wrong in similar places.

items.title: Benchmarking and Domain Adaptation of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) for Adolescent Health Communication in Ghanaian Languages
items.summary: This paper presents an end-to-end study benchmarking five Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems and their domain adaptation for adolescent health communication in three Ghanaian languages (Twi, Dagbani, and Ewe).

items.title: UltraBench 2: Towards Robust Evaluation of Vision Foundation Models on Ultrasound
items.summary: This paper discusses UltraBench 2, focusing on the critical need for and development of robust benchmarks to evaluate vision foundation models specifically for ultrasound applications.

items.title: CinematicVQA: Benchmarking Film-Grammar Reasoning in Large Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Introduces CinematicVQA, a new benchmark designed to evaluate and measure Large Vision-Language Models' reasoning capabilities regarding film grammar and cinematography.

items.title: Beneath the Scores: Rethinking Hallucination Evaluation for Video Understanding Models
items.summary: Proposes rethinking hallucination evaluation for multi-stage LLM agents in video understanding models, aiming to identify where hallucinations originate by analyzing different stages.

items.title: RGBD20K: A Large-Scale Benchmark for RGB-D Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: Proposes RGBD20K, a novel large-scale dataset designed to serve as a benchmark for RGB-D semantic segmentation, featuring abundant categories and high-quality annotations.

items.title: SEE Challenge 2026: Event-Guided Brightness Adjustment Across a Broad Illumination Range
items.summary: The SEE Challenge 2026 was organized to benchmark event-guided brightness adjustment methods across a broad illumination range. It evaluates the restoration capabilities of techniques utilizing event cameras, which excel in high dynamic range conditions.
